<a id="gETAuthorizeDBSecurityGroupIngress"></a>
# **gETAuthorizeDBSecurityGroupIngress**
> AuthorizeDBSecurityGroupIngressResult gETAuthorizeDBSecurityGroupIngress(dbSecurityGroupName, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, CIDRIP, ec2SecurityGroupName, ec2SecurityGroupId, ec2SecurityGroupOwnerId)



&lt;p&gt;Enables ingress to a DBSecurityGroup using one of two forms of authorization. First, EC2 or VPC security groups can be added to the DBSecurityGroup if the application using the database is running on EC2 or VPC instances. Second, IP ranges are available if the application accessing your database is running on the internet. Required parameters for this API are one of CIDR range, EC2SecurityGroupId for VPC, or (EC2SecurityGroupOwnerId and either EC2SecurityGroupName or EC2SecurityGroupId for non-VPC).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;You can&#39;t authorize ingress from an EC2 security group in one Amazon Web Services Region to an Amazon RDS DB instance in another. You can&#39;t authorize ingress from a VPC security group in one VPC to an Amazon RDS DB instance in another.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For an overview of CIDR ranges, go to the &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classless_Inter-Domain_Routing\&quot;&gt;Wikipedia Tutorial&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;EC2-Classic was retired on August 15, 2022. If you haven&#39;t migrated from EC2-Classic to a VPC, we recommend that you migrate as soon as possible. For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/vpc-migrate.html\&quot;&gt;Migrate from EC2-Classic to a VPC&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon EC2 User Guide&lt;/i&gt;, the blog &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;http://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/ec2-classic-is-retiring-heres-how-to-prepare/\&quot;&gt;EC2-Classic Networking is Retiring – Here’s How to Prepare&lt;/a&gt;, and &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_VPC.Non-VPC2VPC.html\&quot;&gt;Moving a DB instance not in a VPC into a VPC&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/note&gt;

In that case, the Amazon Web Services Region where you call the &lt;code&gt;CopyDBClusterSnapshot&lt;/code&gt; operation is the destination Amazon Web Services Region for the encrypted DB cluster snapshot to be copied to. To copy an encrypted DB cluster snapshot from another Amazon Web Services Region, you must provide the following values:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;KmsKeyId&lt;/code&gt; - The Amazon Web Services Key Management System (Amazon Web Services KMS) key identifier for the key to use to encrypt the copy of the DB cluster snapshot in the destination Amazon Web Services Region.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;TargetDBClusterSnapshotIdentifier&lt;/code&gt; - The identifier for the new copy of the DB cluster snapshot in the destination Amazon Web Services Region.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;SourceDBClusterSnapshotIdentifier&lt;/code&gt; - The DB cluster snapshot identifier for the encrypted DB cluster snapshot to be copied. This identifier must be in the ARN format for the source Amazon Web Services Region and is the same value as the &lt;code&gt;SourceDBClusterSnapshotIdentifier&lt;/code&gt; in the presigned URL.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;To cancel the copy operation once it is in progress, delete the target DB cluster snapshot identified by &lt;code&gt;TargetDBClusterSnapshotIdentifier&lt;/code&gt; while that DB cluster snapshot is in \&quot;copying\&quot; status.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on copying encrypted Amazon Aurora DB cluster snapshots from one Amazon Web Services Region to another, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/USER_CopySnapshot.html\&quot;&gt; Copying a Snapshot&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on Amazon Aurora DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html\&quot;&gt; What is Amazon Aurora?&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on Multi-AZ DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/multi-az-db-clusters-concepts.html\&quot;&gt; Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

<a id="gETCreateBlueGreenDeployment"></a>
# **gETCreateBlueGreenDeployment**
> CreateBlueGreenDeploymentResponse gETCreateBlueGreenDeployment(blueGreenDeploymentName, source, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, targetEngineVersion, targetDBParameterGroupName, targetDBClusterParameterGroupName, tags)



&lt;p&gt;Creates a blue/green deployment.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;A blue/green deployment creates a staging environment that copies the production environment. In a blue/green deployment, the blue environment is the current production environment. The green environment is the staging environment. The staging environment stays in sync with the current production environment using logical replication.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;You can make changes to the databases in the green environment without affecting production workloads. For example, you can upgrade the major or minor DB engine version, change database parameters, or make schema changes in the staging environment. You can thoroughly test changes in the green environment. When ready, you can switch over the environments to promote the green environment to be the new production environment. The switchover typically takes under a minute.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/blue-green-deployments.html\&quot;&gt;Using Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments for database updates&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt; and &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/blue-green-deployments.html\&quot;&gt; Using Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments for database updates&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

# **gETCreateDBCluster**
> CreateDBClusterResult gETCreateDBCluster(dbClusterIdentifier, engine, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, availabilityZones, backupRetentionPeriod, characterSetName, databaseName, dbClusterParameterGroupName, vpcSecurityGroupIds, dbSubnetGroupName, engineVersion, port, masterUsername, masterUserPassword, optionGroupName, preferredBackupWindow, preferredMaintenanceWindow, replicationSourceIdentifier, tags, storageEncrypted, kmsKeyId, preSignedUrl, enableIAMDatabaseAuthentication, backtrackWindow, enableCloudwatchLogsExports, engineMode, scalingConfiguration, deletionProtection, globalClusterIdentifier, enableHttpEndpoint, copyTagsToSnapshot, domain, domainIAMRoleName, enableGlobalWriteForwarding, dbClusterInstanceClass, allocatedStorage, storageType, iops, publiclyAccessible, autoMinorVersionUpgrade, monitoringInterval, monitoringRoleArn, enablePerformanceInsights, performanceInsightsKMSKeyId, performanceInsightsRetentionPeriod, serverlessV2ScalingConfiguration, networkType, dbSystemId, manageMasterUserPassword, masterUserSecretKmsKeyId, enableLocalWriteForwarding, sourceRegion)



&lt;p&gt;Creates a new Amazon Aurora DB cluster or Multi-AZ DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you create an Aurora DB cluster, the request creates an empty cluster. You must explicitly create the writer instance for your DB cluster using the &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/APIReference/API_CreateDBInstance.html\&quot;&gt;CreateDBInstance&lt;/a&gt; operation. If you create a Multi-AZ DB cluster, the request creates a writer and two reader DB instances for you, each in a different Availability Zone.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;You can use the &lt;code&gt;ReplicationSourceIdentifier&lt;/code&gt; parameter to create an Amazon Aurora DB cluster as a read replica of another DB cluster or Amazon RDS for MySQL or PostgreSQL DB instance. For more information about Amazon Aurora, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html\&quot;&gt;What is Amazon Aurora?&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;You can also use the &lt;code&gt;ReplicationSourceIdentifier&lt;/code&gt; parameter to create a Multi-AZ DB cluster read replica with an RDS for MySQL or PostgreSQL DB instance as the source. For more information about Multi-AZ DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/multi-az-db-clusters-concepts.html\&quot;&gt;Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

| **xAmzSignature** | **String**|  | [optional] |
| **xAmzSignedHeaders** | **String**|  | [optional] |
| **availabilityZones** | [**List&lt;String&gt;**](String.md)| &lt;p&gt;A list of Availability Zones (AZs) where DB instances in the DB cluster can be created.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For information on Amazon Web Services Regions and Availability Zones, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.RegionsAndAvailabilityZones.html\&quot;&gt;Choosing the Regions and Availability Zones&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **backupRetentionPeriod** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The number of days for which automated backups are retained.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;1&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be a value from 1 to 35.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **characterSetName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The name of the character set (&lt;code&gt;CharacterSet&lt;/code&gt;) to associate the DB cluster with.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **databaseName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The name for your database of up to 64 alphanumeric characters. If you don&#39;t provide a name, Amazon RDS doesn&#39;t create a database in the DB cluster you are creating.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **dbClusterParameterGroupName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The name of the DB cluster parameter group to associate with this DB cluster. If you don&#39;t specify a value, then the default DB cluster parameter group for the specified DB engine and version is used.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If supplied, must match the name of an existing DB cluster parameter group.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **vpcSecurityGroupIds** | [**List&lt;String&gt;**](String.md)| &lt;p&gt;A list of EC2 VPC security groups to associate with this DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **dbSubnetGroupName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;A DB subnet group to associate with this DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting is required to create a Multi-AZ DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must match the name of an existing DB subnet group.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must not be &lt;code&gt;default&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Example: &lt;code&gt;mydbsubnetgroup&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **engineVersion** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The version number of the database engine to use.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;To list all of the available engine versions for Aurora MySQL version 2 (5.7-compatible) and version 3 (MySQL 8.0-compatible), use the following command:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;aws rds describe-db-engine-versions --engine aurora-mysql --query \&quot;DBEngineVersions[].EngineVersion\&quot;&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;You can supply either &lt;code&gt;5.7&lt;/code&gt; or &lt;code&gt;8.0&lt;/code&gt; to use the default engine version for Aurora MySQL version 2 or version 3, respectively.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;To list all of the available engine versions for Aurora PostgreSQL, use the following command:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;aws rds describe-db-engine-versions --engine aurora-postgresql --query \&quot;DBEngineVersions[].EngineVersion\&quot;&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;To list all of the available engine versions for RDS for MySQL, use the following command:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;aws rds describe-db-engine-versions --engine mysql --query \&quot;DBEngineVersions[].EngineVersion\&quot;&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;To list all of the available engine versions for RDS for PostgreSQL, use the following command:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;aws rds describe-db-engine-versions --engine postgres --query \&quot;DBEngineVersions[].EngineVersion\&quot;&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For information about a specific engine, see the following topics:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Aurora MySQL - see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraMySQL.Updates.html\&quot;&gt;Database engine updates for Amazon Aurora MySQL&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Aurora PostgreSQL - see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraPostgreSQL.Updates.20180305.html\&quot;&gt;Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL releases and engine versions&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for MySQL - see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_MySQL.html#MySQL.Concepts.VersionMgmt\&quot;&gt;Amazon RDS for MySQL&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for PostgreSQL - see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_PostgreSQL.html#PostgreSQL.Concepts\&quot;&gt;Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **port** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The port number on which the instances in the DB cluster accept connections.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values: &lt;code&gt;1150-65535&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for MySQL and Aurora MySQL - &lt;code&gt;3306&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for PostgreSQL and Aurora PostgreSQL - &lt;code&gt;5432&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **masterUsername** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The name of the master user for the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be 1 to 16 letters or numbers.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;First character must be a letter.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can&#39;t be a reserved word for the chosen database engine.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **masterUserPassword** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The password for the master database user.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must contain from 8 to 41 characters.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can contain any printable ASCII character except \&quot;/\&quot;, \&quot;\&quot;\&quot;, or \&quot;@\&quot;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can&#39;t be specified if &lt;code&gt;ManageMasterUserPassword&lt;/code&gt; is turned on.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **optionGroupName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The option group to associate the DB cluster with.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;DB clusters are associated with a default option group that can&#39;t be modified.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **preferredBackupWindow** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The daily time range during which automated backups are created if automated backups are enabled using the &lt;code&gt;BackupRetentionPeriod&lt;/code&gt; parameter.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The default is a 30-minute window selected at random from an 8-hour block of time for each Amazon Web Services Region. To view the time blocks available, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Managing.Backups.html#Aurora.Managing.Backups.BackupWindow\&quot;&gt; Backup window&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be in the format &lt;code&gt;hh24:mi-hh24:mi&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be in Universal Coordinated Time (UTC).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must not conflict with the preferred maintenance window.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be at least 30 minutes.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **preferredMaintenanceWindow** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The weekly time range during which system maintenance can occur.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The default is a 30-minute window selected at random from an 8-hour block of time for each Amazon Web Services Region, occurring on a random day of the week. To see the time blocks available, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/USER_UpgradeDBInstance.Maintenance.html#AdjustingTheMaintenanceWindow.Aurora\&quot;&gt; Adjusting the Preferred DB Cluster Maintenance Window&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be in the format &lt;code&gt;ddd:hh24:mi-ddd:hh24:mi&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Days must be one of &lt;code&gt;Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri | Sat | Sun&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be in Universal Coordinated Time (UTC).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be at least 30 minutes.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **replicationSourceIdentifier** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the source DB instance or DB cluster if this DB cluster is created as a read replica.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **tags** | [**List&lt;Tag&gt;**](Tag.md)| &lt;p&gt;Tags to assign to the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **storageEncrypted** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether the DB cluster is encrypted.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **kmsKeyId** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier for an encrypted DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier is the key ARN, key ID, alias ARN, or alias name for the KMS key. To use a KMS key in a different Amazon Web Services account, specify the key ARN or alias ARN.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When a KMS key isn&#39;t specified in &lt;code&gt;KmsKeyId&lt;/code&gt;:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;ReplicationSourceIdentifier&lt;/code&gt; identifies an encrypted source, then Amazon RDS uses the KMS key used to encrypt the source. Otherwise, Amazon RDS uses your default KMS key.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the &lt;code&gt;StorageEncrypted&lt;/code&gt; parameter is enabled and &lt;code&gt;ReplicationSourceIdentifier&lt;/code&gt; isn&#39;t specified, then Amazon RDS uses your default KMS key.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;There is a default KMS key for your Amazon Web Services account. Your Amazon Web Services account has a different default KMS key for each Amazon Web Services Region.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you create a read replica of an encrypted DB cluster in another Amazon Web Services Region, make sure to set &lt;code&gt;KmsKeyId&lt;/code&gt; to a KMS key identifier that is valid in the destination Amazon Web Services Region. This KMS key is used to encrypt the read replica in that Amazon Web Services Region.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **preSignedUrl** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;When you are replicating a DB cluster from one Amazon Web Services GovCloud (US) Region to another, an URL that contains a Signature Version 4 signed request for the &lt;code&gt;CreateDBCluster&lt;/code&gt; operation to be called in the source Amazon Web Services Region where the DB cluster is replicated from. Specify &lt;code&gt;PreSignedUrl&lt;/code&gt; only when you are performing cross-Region replication from an encrypted DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The presigned URL must be a valid request for the &lt;code&gt;CreateDBCluster&lt;/code&gt; API operation that can run in the source Amazon Web Services Region that contains the encrypted DB cluster to copy.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The presigned URL request must contain the following parameter values:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;KmsKeyId&lt;/code&gt; - The KMS key identifier for the KMS key to use to encrypt the copy of the DB cluster in the destination Amazon Web Services Region. This should refer to the same KMS key for both the &lt;code&gt;CreateDBCluster&lt;/code&gt; operation that is called in the destination Amazon Web Services Region, and the operation contained in the presigned URL.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;DestinationRegion&lt;/code&gt; - The name of the Amazon Web Services Region that Aurora read replica will be created in.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;ReplicationSourceIdentifier&lt;/code&gt; - The DB cluster identifier for the encrypted DB cluster to be copied. This identifier must be in the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) format for the source Amazon Web Services Region. For example, if you are copying an encrypted DB cluster from the us-west-2 Amazon Web Services Region, then your &lt;code&gt;ReplicationSourceIdentifier&lt;/code&gt; would look like Example: &lt;code&gt;arn:aws:rds:us-west-2:123456789012:cluster:aurora-cluster1&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;To learn how to generate a Signature Version 4 signed request, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/sigv4-query-string-auth.html\&quot;&gt; Authenticating Requests: Using Query Parameters (Amazon Web Services Signature Version 4)&lt;/a&gt; and &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/signature-version-4.html\&quot;&gt; Signature Version 4 Signing Process&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you are using an Amazon Web Services SDK tool or the CLI, you can specify &lt;code&gt;SourceRegion&lt;/code&gt; (or &lt;code&gt;--source-region&lt;/code&gt; for the CLI) instead of specifying &lt;code&gt;PreSignedUrl&lt;/code&gt; manually. Specifying &lt;code&gt;SourceRegion&lt;/code&gt; autogenerates a presigned URL that is a valid request for the operation that can run in the source Amazon Web Services Region.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/note&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt;&lt;note&gt;&lt;p&gt;If you supply a value for this operation&#39;s &lt;code&gt;SourceRegion&lt;/code&gt; parameter, a pre-signed URL will be calculated on your behalf.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/note&gt; | [optional] |
| **enableIAMDatabaseAuthentication** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to enable mapping of Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management (IAM) accounts to database accounts. By default, mapping isn&#39;t enabled.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/UsingWithRDS.IAMDBAuth.html\&quot;&gt; IAM Database Authentication&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **backtrackWindow** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The target backtrack window, in seconds. To disable backtracking, set this value to &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora MySQL DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If specified, this value must be set to a number from 0 to 259,200 (72 hours).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **enableCloudwatchLogsExports** | [**List&lt;String&gt;**](String.md)| &lt;p&gt;The list of log types that need to be enabled for exporting to CloudWatch Logs.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The following values are valid for each DB engine:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Aurora MySQL - &lt;code&gt;audit | error | general | slowquery&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Aurora PostgreSQL - &lt;code&gt;postgresql&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for MySQL - &lt;code&gt;error | general | slowquery&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for PostgreSQL - &lt;code&gt;postgresql | upgrade&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information about exporting CloudWatch Logs for Amazon RDS, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_LogAccess.html#USER_LogAccess.Procedural.UploadtoCloudWatch\&quot;&gt;Publishing Database Logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information about exporting CloudWatch Logs for Amazon Aurora, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/USER_LogAccess.html#USER_LogAccess.Procedural.UploadtoCloudWatch\&quot;&gt;Publishing Database Logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **engineMode** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The DB engine mode of the DB cluster, either &lt;code&gt;provisioned&lt;/code&gt; or &lt;code&gt;serverless&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The &lt;code&gt;serverless&lt;/code&gt; engine mode only applies for Aurora Serverless v1 DB clusters.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For information about limitations and requirements for Serverless DB clusters, see the following sections in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless.html#aurora-serverless.limitations\&quot;&gt;Limitations of Aurora Serverless v1&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.requirements.html\&quot;&gt;Requirements for Aurora Serverless v2&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **scalingConfiguration** | [**GETCreateDBClusterScalingConfigurationParameter**](.md)| &lt;p&gt;For DB clusters in &lt;code&gt;serverless&lt;/code&gt; DB engine mode, the scaling properties of the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **deletionProtection** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether the DB cluster has deletion protection enabled. The database can&#39;t be deleted when deletion protection is enabled. By default, deletion protection isn&#39;t enabled.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **globalClusterIdentifier** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The global cluster ID of an Aurora cluster that becomes the primary cluster in the new global database cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **enableHttpEndpoint** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to enable the HTTP endpoint for an Aurora Serverless v1 DB cluster. By default, the HTTP endpoint is disabled.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When enabled, the HTTP endpoint provides a connectionless web service API for running SQL queries on the Aurora Serverless v1 DB cluster. You can also query your database from inside the RDS console with the query editor.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/data-api.html\&quot;&gt;Using the Data API for Aurora Serverless v1&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **copyTagsToSnapshot** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to copy all tags from the DB cluster to snapshots of the DB cluster. The default is not to copy them.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **domain** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Active Directory directory ID to create the DB cluster in.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For Amazon Aurora DB clusters, Amazon RDS can use Kerberos authentication to authenticate users that connect to the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/kerberos-authentication.html\&quot;&gt;Kerberos authentication&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **domainIAMRoleName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The name of the IAM role to use when making API calls to the Directory Service.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **enableGlobalWriteForwarding** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to enable this DB cluster to forward write operations to the primary cluster of a global cluster (Aurora global database). By default, write operations are not allowed on Aurora DB clusters that are secondary clusters in an Aurora global database.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;You can set this value only on Aurora DB clusters that are members of an Aurora global database. With this parameter enabled, a secondary cluster can forward writes to the current primary cluster, and the resulting changes are replicated back to this cluster. For the primary DB cluster of an Aurora global database, this value is used immediately if the primary is demoted by a global cluster API operation, but it does nothing until then.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **dbClusterInstanceClass** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The compute and memory capacity of each DB instance in the Multi-AZ DB cluster, for example &lt;code&gt;db.m6gd.xlarge&lt;/code&gt;. Not all DB instance classes are available in all Amazon Web Services Regions, or for all database engines.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For the full list of DB instance classes and availability for your engine, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.DBInstanceClass.html\&quot;&gt;DB instance class&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting is required to create a Multi-AZ DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **allocatedStorage** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The amount of storage in gibibytes (GiB) to allocate to each DB instance in the Multi-AZ DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting is required to create a Multi-AZ DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **storageType** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The storage type to associate with the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For information on storage types for Aurora DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Overview.StorageReliability.html#aurora-storage-type\&quot;&gt;Storage configurations for Amazon Aurora DB clusters&lt;/a&gt;. For information on storage types for Multi-AZ DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/create-multi-az-db-cluster.html#create-multi-az-db-cluster-settings\&quot;&gt;Settings for creating Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting is required to create a Multi-AZ DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When specified for a Multi-AZ DB cluster, a value for the &lt;code&gt;Iops&lt;/code&gt; parameter is required.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Aurora DB clusters - &lt;code&gt;aurora | aurora-iopt1&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Multi-AZ DB clusters - &lt;code&gt;io1&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Aurora DB clusters - &lt;code&gt;aurora&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Multi-AZ DB clusters - &lt;code&gt;io1&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **iops** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The amount of Provisioned IOPS (input/output operations per second) to be initially allocated for each DB instance in the Multi-AZ DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For information about valid IOPS values, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_Storage.html#USER_PIOPS\&quot;&gt;Provisioned IOPS storage&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting is required to create a Multi-AZ DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be a multiple between .5 and 50 of the storage amount for the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **publiclyAccessible** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether the DB cluster is publicly accessible.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When the DB cluster is publicly accessible, its Domain Name System (DNS) endpoint resolves to the private IP address from within the DB cluster&#39;s virtual private cloud (VPC). It resolves to the public IP address from outside of the DB cluster&#39;s VPC. Access to the DB cluster is ultimately controlled by the security group it uses. That public access isn&#39;t permitted if the security group assigned to the DB cluster doesn&#39;t permit it.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When the DB cluster isn&#39;t publicly accessible, it is an internal DB cluster with a DNS name that resolves to a private IP address.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: The default behavior varies depending on whether &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroupName&lt;/code&gt; is specified.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroupName&lt;/code&gt; isn&#39;t specified, and &lt;code&gt;PubliclyAccessible&lt;/code&gt; isn&#39;t specified, the following applies:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the default VPC in the target Region doesn’t have an internet gateway attached to it, the DB cluster is private.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the default VPC in the target Region has an internet gateway attached to it, the DB cluster is public.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroupName&lt;/code&gt; is specified, and &lt;code&gt;PubliclyAccessible&lt;/code&gt; isn&#39;t specified, the following applies:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the subnets are part of a VPC that doesn’t have an internet gateway attached to it, the DB cluster is private.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the subnets are part of a VPC that has an internet gateway attached to it, the DB cluster is public.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **autoMinorVersionUpgrade** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether minor engine upgrades are applied automatically to the DB cluster during the maintenance window. By default, minor engine upgrades are applied automatically.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **monitoringInterval** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The interval, in seconds, between points when Enhanced Monitoring metrics are collected for the DB cluster. To turn off collecting Enhanced Monitoring metrics, specify &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;MonitoringRoleArn&lt;/code&gt; is specified, also set &lt;code&gt;MonitoringInterval&lt;/code&gt; to a value other than &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values: &lt;code&gt;0 | 1 | 5 | 10 | 15 | 30 | 60&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **monitoringRoleArn** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the IAM role that permits RDS to send Enhanced Monitoring metrics to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. An example is &lt;code&gt;arn:aws:iam:123456789012:role/emaccess&lt;/code&gt;. For information on creating a monitoring role, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_Monitoring.OS.html#USER_Monitoring.OS.Enabling\&quot;&gt;Setting up and enabling Enhanced Monitoring&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;MonitoringInterval&lt;/code&gt; is set to a value other than &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;, supply a &lt;code&gt;MonitoringRoleArn&lt;/code&gt; value.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **enablePerformanceInsights** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to turn on Performance Insights for the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PerfInsights.html\&quot;&gt; Using Amazon Performance Insights&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **performanceInsightsKMSKeyId** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier for encryption of Performance Insights data.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier is the key ARN, key ID, alias ARN, or alias name for the KMS key.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you don&#39;t specify a value for &lt;code&gt;PerformanceInsightsKMSKeyId&lt;/code&gt;, then Amazon RDS uses your default KMS key. There is a default KMS key for your Amazon Web Services account. Your Amazon Web Services account has a different default KMS key for each Amazon Web Services Region.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **performanceInsightsRetentionPeriod** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The number of days to retain Performance Insights data.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;7&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;i&gt;month&lt;/i&gt; * 31, where &lt;i&gt;month&lt;/i&gt; is a number of months from 1-23. Examples: &lt;code&gt;93&lt;/code&gt; (3 months * 31), &lt;code&gt;341&lt;/code&gt; (11 months * 31), &lt;code&gt;589&lt;/code&gt; (19 months * 31)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;731&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;7&lt;/code&gt; days&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you specify a retention period that isn&#39;t valid, such as &lt;code&gt;94&lt;/code&gt;, Amazon RDS issues an error.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **serverlessV2ScalingConfiguration** | [**GETCreateDBClusterServerlessV2ScalingConfigurationParameter**](.md)|  | [optional] |
| **networkType** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The network type of the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The network type is determined by the &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroup&lt;/code&gt; specified for the DB cluster. A &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroup&lt;/code&gt; can support only the IPv4 protocol or the IPv4 and the IPv6 protocols (&lt;code&gt;DUAL&lt;/code&gt;).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/USER_VPC.WorkingWithRDSInstanceinaVPC.html\&quot;&gt; Working with a DB instance in a VPC&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values: &lt;code&gt;IPV4 | DUAL&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **dbSystemId** | **String**| Reserved for future use. | [optional] |
| **manageMasterUserPassword** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to manage the master user password with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html\&quot;&gt;Password management with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt; and &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html\&quot;&gt;Password management with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can&#39;t manage the master user password with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager if &lt;code&gt;MasterUserPassword&lt;/code&gt; is specified.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **masterUserSecretKmsKeyId** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier to encrypt a secret that is automatically generated and managed in Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting is valid only if the master user password is managed by RDS in Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager for the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier is the key ARN, key ID, alias ARN, or alias name for the KMS key. To use a KMS key in a different Amazon Web Services account, specify the key ARN or alias ARN.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you don&#39;t specify &lt;code&gt;MasterUserSecretKmsKeyId&lt;/code&gt;, then the &lt;code&gt;aws/secretsmanager&lt;/code&gt; KMS key is used to encrypt the secret. If the secret is in a different Amazon Web Services account, then you can&#39;t use the &lt;code&gt;aws/secretsmanager&lt;/code&gt; KMS key to encrypt the secret, and you must use a customer managed KMS key.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;There is a default KMS key for your Amazon Web Services account. Your Amazon Web Services account has a different default KMS key for each Amazon Web Services Region.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **enableLocalWriteForwarding** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether read replicas can forward write operations to the writer DB instance in the DB cluster. By default, write operations aren&#39;t allowed on reader DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **sourceRegion** | **String**| The ID of the region that contains the source for the read replica. | [optional] |

<a id="gETCreateDBClusterParameterGroup"></a>
# **gETCreateDBClusterParameterGroup**
> CreateDBClusterParameterGroupResult gETCreateDBClusterParameterGroup(dbClusterParameterGroupName, dbParameterGroupFamily, description, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, tags)



&lt;p&gt;Creates a new DB cluster parameter group.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Parameters in a DB cluster parameter group apply to all of the instances in a DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;A DB cluster parameter group is initially created with the default parameters for the database engine used by instances in the DB cluster. To provide custom values for any of the parameters, you must modify the group after creating it using &lt;code&gt;ModifyDBClusterParameterGroup&lt;/code&gt;. Once you&#39;ve created a DB cluster parameter group, you need to associate it with your DB cluster using &lt;code&gt;ModifyDBCluster&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When you associate a new DB cluster parameter group with a running Aurora DB cluster, reboot the DB instances in the DB cluster without failover for the new DB cluster parameter group and associated settings to take effect.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When you associate a new DB cluster parameter group with a running Multi-AZ DB cluster, reboot the DB cluster without failover for the new DB cluster parameter group and associated settings to take effect.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;important&gt; &lt;p&gt;After you create a DB cluster parameter group, you should wait at least 5 minutes before creating your first DB cluster that uses that DB cluster parameter group as the default parameter group. This allows Amazon RDS to fully complete the create action before the DB cluster parameter group is used as the default for a new DB cluster. This is especially important for parameters that are critical when creating the default database for a DB cluster, such as the character set for the default database defined by the &lt;code&gt;character_set_database&lt;/code&gt; parameter. You can use the &lt;i&gt;Parameter Groups&lt;/i&gt; option of the &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://console.aws.amazon.com/rds/\&quot;&gt;Amazon RDS console&lt;/a&gt; or the &lt;code&gt;DescribeDBClusterParameters&lt;/code&gt; operation to verify that your DB cluster parameter group has been created or modified.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/important&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on Amazon Aurora, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html\&quot;&gt; What is Amazon Aurora?&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on Multi-AZ DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/multi-az-db-clusters-concepts.html\&quot;&gt; Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

### Example
```java

    defaultClient.setBasePath("http://rds.us-east-1.amazonaws.com");
    
    // Configure API key authorization: hmac
    ApiKeyAuth hmac = (ApiKeyAuth) defaultClient.getAuthentication("hmac");
    hmac.setApiKey("YOUR API KEY");
    // Uncomment the following line to set a prefix for the API key, e.g. "Token" (defaults to null)
    //hmac.setApiKeyPrefix("Token");

    DefaultApi apiInstance = new DefaultApi(defaultClient);

be an integer from 20 to 65536.</p> </li> <li> <p>Provisioned IOPS storage (io1): Must be an integer from 100 to 65536.</p> </li> <li> <p>Magnetic storage (standard): Must be an integer from 5 to 3072.</p> </li> </ul> </dd> <dt>RDS for Oracle</dt> <dd> <p>Constraints to the amount of storage for each storage type are the following:</p> <ul> <li> <p>General Purpose (SSD) storage (gp2, gp3): Must be an integer from 20 to 65536.</p> </li> <li> <p>Provisioned IOPS storage (io1): Must be an integer from 100 to 65536.</p> </li> <li> <p>Magnetic storage (standard): Must be an integer from 10 to 3072.</p> </li> </ul> </dd> <dt>RDS for PostgreSQL</dt> <dd> <p>Constraints to the amount of storage for each storage type are the following:</p> <ul> <li> <p>General Purpose (SSD) storage (gp2, gp3): Must be an integer from 20 to 65536.</p> </li> <li> <p>Provisioned IOPS storage (io1): Must be an integer from 100 to 65536.</p> </li> <li> <p>Magnetic storage (standard): Must be an integer from 5 to 3072.</p> </li> </ul> </dd> <dt>RDS for SQL Server</dt> <dd> <p>Constraints to the amount of storage for each storage type are the following:</p> <ul> <li> <p>General Purpose (SSD) storage (gp2, gp3):</p> <ul> <li> <p>Enterprise and Standard editions: Must be an integer from 20 to 16384.</p> </li> <li> <p>Web and Express editions: Must be an integer from 20 to 16384.</p> </li> </ul> </li> <li> <p>Provisioned IOPS storage (io1):</p> <ul> <li> <p>Enterprise and Standard editions: Must be an integer from 100 to 16384.</p> </li> <li> <p>Web and Express editions: Must be an integer from 100 to 16384.</p> </li> </ul> </li> <li> <p>Magnetic storage (standard):</p> <ul> <li> <p>Enterprise and Standard editions: Must be an integer from 20 to 1024.</p> </li> <li> <p>Web and Express editions: Must be an integer from 20 to 1024.</p> </li> </ul> </li> </ul> </dd> </dl>
    String masterUsername = "masterUsername_example"; // String | <p>The name for the master user.</p> <p>This setting doesn't apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. The name for the master user is managed by the DB cluster.</p> <p>This setting is required for RDS DB instances.</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Must be 1 to 16 letters, numbers, or underscores.</p> </li> <li> <p>First character must be a letter.</p> </li> <li> <p>Can't be a reserved word for the chosen database engine.</p> </li> </ul>
    String masterUserPassword = "masterUserPassword_example"; // String | <p>The password for the master user.</p> <p>This setting doesn't apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. The password for the master user is managed by the DB cluster.</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Can't be specified if <code>ManageMasterUserPassword</code> is turned on.</p> </li> <li> <p>Can include any printable ASCII character except \"/\", \"\"\", or \"@\".</p> </li> </ul> <p>Length Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>RDS for MariaDB - Must contain from 8 to 41 characters.</p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for Microsoft SQL Server - Must contain from 8 to 128 characters.</p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for MySQL - Must contain from 8 to 41 characters.</p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for Oracle - Must contain from 8 to 30 characters.</p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for PostgreSQL - Must contain from 8 to 128 characters.</p> </li> </ul>
    List<String> dbSecurityGroups = Arrays.asList(); // List<String> | <p>A list of DB security groups to associate with this DB instance.</p> <p>This setting applies to the legacy EC2-Classic platform, which is no longer used to create new DB instances. Use the <code>VpcSecurityGroupIds</code> setting instead.</p>
    List<String> vpcSecurityGroupIds = Arrays.asList(); // List<String> | <p>A list of Amazon EC2 VPC security groups to associate with this DB instance.</p> <p>This setting doesn't apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. The associated list of EC2 VPC security groups is managed by the DB cluster.</p> <p>Default: The default EC2 VPC security group for the DB subnet group's VPC.</p>
    String availabilityZone = "availabilityZone_example"; // String | <p>The Availability Zone (AZ) where the database will be created. For information on Amazon Web Services Regions and Availability Zones, see <a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.RegionsAndAvailabilityZones.html\">Regions and Availability Zones</a>.</p> <p>For Amazon Aurora, each Aurora DB cluster hosts copies of its storage in three separate Availability Zones. Specify one of these Availability Zones. Aurora automatically chooses an appropriate Availability Zone if you don't specify one.</p> <p>Default: A random, system-chosen Availability Zone in the endpoint's Amazon Web Services Region.</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>The <code>AvailabilityZone</code> parameter can't be specified if the DB instance is a Multi-AZ deployment.</p> </li> <li> <p>The specified Availability Zone must be in the same Amazon Web Services Region as the current endpoint.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Example: <code>us-east-1d</code> </p>
    String dbSubnetGroupName = "dbSubnetGroupName_example"; // String | <p>A DB subnet group to associate with this DB instance.</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Must match the name of an existing DB subnet group.</p> </li> <li> <p>Must not be <code>default</code>.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Example: <code>mydbsubnetgroup</code> </p>
    String preferredMaintenanceWindow = "preferredMaintenanceWindow_example"; // String | <p>The time range each week during which system maintenance can occur. For more information, see <a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_UpgradeDBInstance.Maintenance.html#Concepts.DBMaintenance\">Amazon RDS Maintenance Window</a> in the <i>Amazon RDS User Guide.</i> </p> <p>The default is a 30-minute window selected at random from an 8-hour block of time for each Amazon Web Services Region, occurring on a random day of the week.</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Must be in the format <code>ddd:hh24:mi-ddd:hh24:mi</code>.</p> </li> <li> <p>The day values must be <code>mon | tue | wed | thu | fri | sat | sun</code>. </p> </li> <li> <p>Must be in Universal Coordinated Time (UTC).</p> </li> <li> <p>Must not conflict with the preferred backup window.</p> </li> <li> <p>Must be at least 30 minutes.</p> </li> </ul>
    String dbParameterGroupName = "dbParameterGroupName_example"; // String | <p>The name of the DB parameter group to associate with this DB instance. If you don't specify a value, then Amazon RDS uses the default DB parameter group for the specified DB engine and version.</p> <p>This setting doesn't apply to RDS Custom DB instances.</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Must be 1 to 255 letters, numbers, or hyphens.</p> </li> <li> <p>The first character must be a letter.</p> </li> <li> <p>Can't end with a hyphen or contain two consecutive hyphens.</p> </li> </ul>
    Integer backupRetentionPeriod = 56; // Integer | <p>The number of days for which automated backups are retained. Setting this parameter to a positive number enables backups. Setting this parameter to <code>0</code> disables automated backups.</p> <p>This setting doesn't apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. The retention period for automated backups is managed by the DB cluster.</p> <p>Default: <code>1</code> </p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Must be a value from 0 to 35.</p> </li> <li> <p>Can't be set to 0 if the DB instance is a source to read replicas.</p> </li> <li> <p>Can't be set to 0 for an RDS Custom for Oracle DB instance.</p> </li> </ul>
    String preferredBackupWindow = "preferredBackupWindow_example"; // String | <p>The daily time range during which automated backups are created if automated backups are enabled, using the <code>BackupRetentionPeriod</code> parameter. The default is a 30-minute window selected at random from an 8-hour block of time for each Amazon Web Services Region. For more information, see <a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.html#USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.BackupWindow\">Backup window</a> in the <i>Amazon RDS User Guide</i>.</p> <p>This setting doesn't apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. The daily time range for creating automated backups is managed by the DB cluster.</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Must be in the format <code>hh24:mi-hh24:mi</code>.</p> </li> <li> <p>Must be in Universal Coordinated Time (UTC).</p> </li> <li> <p>Must not conflict with the preferred maintenance window.</p> </li> <li> <p>Must be at least 30 minutes.</p> </li> </ul>
    Integer port = 56; // Integer | <p>The port number on which the database accepts connections.</p> <p>This setting doesn't apply to Aurora DB instances. The port number is managed by the cluster.</p> <p>Valid Values: <code>1150-65535</code> </p> <p>Default:</p> <ul> <li> <p>RDS for MariaDB - <code>3306</code> </p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for Microsoft SQL Server - <code>1433</code> </p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for MySQL - <code>3306</code> </p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for Oracle - <code>1521</code> </p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for PostgreSQL - <code>5432</code> </p> </li> </ul> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>For RDS for Microsoft SQL Server, the value can't be <code>1234</code>, <code>1434</code>, <code>3260</code>, <code>3343</code>, <code>3389</code>, <code>47001</code>, or <code>49152-49156</code>.</p> </li> </ul>
    Boolean multiAZ = true; // Boolean | <p>Specifies whether the DB instance is a Multi-AZ deployment. You can't set the <code>AvailabilityZone</code> parameter if the DB instance is a Multi-AZ deployment.</p> <p>This setting doesn't apply to the following DB instances:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Amazon Aurora (DB instance Availability Zones (AZs) are managed by the DB cluster.)</p> </li> <li> <p>RDS Custom</p> </li> </ul>
    String engineVersion = "engineVersion_example"; // String | <p>The version number of the database engine to use.</p> <p>This setting doesn't apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. The version number of the database engine the DB instance uses is managed by the DB cluster.</p> <p>For a list of valid engine versions, use the <code>DescribeDBEngineVersions</code> operation.</p> <p>The following are the database engines and links to information about the major and minor versions that are available with Amazon RDS. Not every database engine is available for every Amazon Web Services Region.</p> <dl> <dt>Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle</dt> <dd> <p>A custom engine version (CEV) that you have previously created. This setting is required for RDS Custom for Oracle. The CEV name has the following format: 19.<i>customized_string</i>. A valid CEV name is <code>19.my_cev1</code>. For more information, see <a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/custom-creating.html#custom-creating.create\"> Creating an RDS Custom for Oracle DB instance</a> in the <i>Amazon RDS User Guide</i>.</p> </dd> <dt>Amazon RDS Custom for SQL Server</dt> <dd> <p>See <a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/custom-reqs-limits-MS.html\">RDS Custom for SQL Server general requirements</a> in the <i>Amazon RDS User Guide</i>.</p> </dd> <dt>RDS for MariaDB</dt> <dd> <p>For information, see <a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_MariaDB.html#MariaDB.Concepts.VersionMgmt\">MariaDB on Amazon RDS versions</a> in the <i>Amazon RDS User Guide</i>.</p> </dd> <dt>RDS for Microsoft SQL Server</dt> <dd> <p>For information, see <a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_SQLServer.html#SQLServer.Concepts.General.VersionSupport\">Microsoft SQL Server versions on Amazon RDS</a> in the <i>Amazon RDS User Guide</i>.</p> </dd> <dt>RDS for MySQL</dt> <dd> <p>For information, see <a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_MySQL.html#MySQL.Concepts.VersionMgmt\">MySQL on Amazon RDS versions</a> in the <i>Amazon RDS User Guide</i>.</p> </dd> <dt>RDS for Oracle</dt> <dd> <p>For information, see <a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Appendix.Oracle.PatchComposition.html\">Oracle Database Engine release notes</a> in the <i>Amazon RDS User Guide</i>.</p> </dd> <dt>RDS for PostgreSQL</dt> <dd> <p>For information, see <a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_PostgreSQL.html#PostgreSQL.Concepts\">Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL versions and extensions</a> in the <i>Amazon RDS User Guide</i>.</p> </dd> </dl>
    Boolean autoMinorVersionUpgrade = true; // Boolean | <p>Specifies whether minor engine upgrades are applied automatically to the DB instance during the maintenance window.     String licenseModel = "licenseModel_example"; // String | <p>The license model information for this DB instance.</p> <p>This setting doesn't apply to Amazon Aurora or RDS Custom DB instances.</p> <p>Valid Values:</p> <ul> <li> <p>RDS for MariaDB - <code>general-public-license</code> </p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for Microsoft SQL Server - <code>license-included</code> </p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for MySQL - <code>general-public-license</code> </p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for Oracle - <code>bring-your-own-license | license-included</code> </p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for PostgreSQL - <code>postgresql-license</code> </p> </li> </ul>

Storage is managed by the DB cluster.</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>For RDS for MariaDB, MySQL, Oracle, and PostgreSQL - Must be a multiple between .5 and 50 of the storage amount for the DB instance.</p> </li> <li> <p>For RDS for SQL Server - Must be a multiple between 1 and 50 of the storage amount for the DB instance.</p> </li> </ul>
    String optionGroupName = "optionGroupName_example"; // String | <p>The option group to associate the DB instance with.</p> <p>Permanent options, such as the TDE option for Oracle Advanced Security TDE, can't be removed from an option group.     String characterSetName = "characterSetName_example"; // String | <p>For supported engines, the character set (<code>CharacterSet</code>) to associate the DB instance with.</p> <p>This setting doesn't apply to the following DB instances:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Amazon Aurora - The character set is managed by the DB cluster.     Boolean publiclyAccessible = true; // Boolean | <p>Specifies whether the DB instance is publicly accessible.</p> <p>When the DB instance is publicly accessible, its Domain Name System (DNS) endpoint resolves to the private IP address from within the DB instance's virtual private cloud (VPC). It resolves to the public IP address from outside of the DB instance's VPC. Access to the DB instance is ultimately controlled by the security group it uses. That public access is not permitted if the security group assigned to the DB instance doesn't permit it.</p> <p>When the DB instance isn't publicly accessible, it is an internal DB instance with a DNS name that resolves to a private IP address.</p> <p>Default: The default behavior varies depending on whether <code>DBSubnetGroupName</code> is specified.</p> <p>If <code>DBSubnetGroupName</code> isn't specified, and <code>PubliclyAccessible</code> isn't specified, the following applies:</p> <ul> <li> <p>If the default VPC in the target Region doesn’t have an internet gateway attached to it, the DB instance is private.</p> </li> <li> <p>If the default VPC in the target Region has an internet gateway attached to it, the DB instance is public.</p> </li> </ul> <p>If <code>DBSubnetGroupName</code> is specified, and <code>PubliclyAccessible</code> isn't specified, the following applies:</p> <ul> <li> <p>If the subnets are part of a VPC that doesn’t have an internet gateway attached to it, the DB instance is private.</p> </li> <li> <p>If the subnets are part of a VPC that has an internet gateway attached to it, the DB instance is public.</p> </li> </ul>

    String tdeCredentialArn = "tdeCredentialArn_example"; // String | <p>The ARN from the key store with which to associate the instance for TDE encryption.</p> <p>This setting doesn't apply to Amazon Aurora or RDS Custom DB instances.</p>

    String kmsKeyId = "kmsKeyId_example"; // String | <p>The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier for an encrypted DB instance.</p> <p>The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier is the key ARN, key ID, alias ARN, or alias name for the KMS key. There is a default KMS key for your Amazon Web Services account. Your Amazon Web Services account has a different default KMS key for each Amazon Web Services Region.</p> <p>For Amazon RDS Custom, a KMS key is required for DB instances. For most RDS engines, if you leave this parameter empty while enabling <code>StorageEncrypted</code>, the engine uses the default KMS key.     String domainFqdn = "domainFqdn_example"; // String | <p>The fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of an Active Directory domain.</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Can't be longer than 64 characters.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Example: <code>mymanagedADtest.mymanagedAD.mydomain</code> </p>

    String domainAuthSecretArn = "domainAuthSecretArn_example"; // String | <p>The ARN for the Secrets Manager secret with the credentials for the user joining the domain.</p> <p>Example: <code>arn:aws:secretsmanager:region:account-number:secret:myselfmanagedADtestsecret-123456</code> </p>
    List<String> domainDnsIps = Arrays.asList(); // List<String> | <p>The IPv4 DNS IP addresses of your primary and secondary Active Directory domain controllers.</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Two IP addresses must be provided.     Integer monitoringInterval = 56; // Integer | <p>The interval, in seconds, between points when Enhanced Monitoring metrics are collected for the DB instance.     String monitoringRoleArn = "monitoringRoleArn_example"; // String | <p>The ARN for the IAM role that permits RDS to send enhanced monitoring metrics to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.     String domainIAMRoleName = "domainIAMRoleName_example"; // String | <p>The name of the IAM role to use when making API calls to the Directory Service.</p> <p>This setting doesn't apply to the following DB instances:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Amazon Aurora (The domain is managed by the DB cluster.)</p> </li> <li> <p>RDS Custom</p> </li> </ul>

    String performanceInsightsKMSKeyId = "performanceInsightsKMSKeyId_example"; // String | <p>The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier for encryption of Performance Insights data.</p> <p>The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier is the key ARN, key ID, alias ARN, or alias name for the KMS key.</p> <p>If you don't specify a value for <code>PerformanceInsightsKMSKeyId</code>, then Amazon RDS uses your default KMS key. There is a default KMS key for your Amazon Web Services account.
