&lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;General Purpose (SSD) storage (gp2, gp3): Must be an integer from 20 to 65536.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Provisioned IOPS storage (io1): Must be an integer from 100 to 65536.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Magnetic storage (standard): Must be an integer from 5 to 3072.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;/dd&gt; &lt;dt&gt;RDS for SQL Server&lt;/dt&gt; &lt;dd&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints to the amount of storage for each storage type are the following:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;General Purpose (SSD) storage (gp2, gp3):&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Enterprise and Standard editions: Must be an integer from 20 to 16384.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Web and Express editions: Must be an integer from 20 to 16384.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Provisioned IOPS storage (io1):&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Enterprise and Standard editions: Must be an integer from 100 to 16384.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Web and Express editions: Must be an integer from 100 to 16384.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Magnetic storage (standard):&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Enterprise and Standard editions: Must be an integer from 20 to 1024.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Web and Express editions: Must be an integer from 20 to 1024.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;/dd&gt; &lt;/dl&gt; | [optional] |
| **masterUsername** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The name for the master user.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. The name for the master user is managed by the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting is required for RDS DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be 1 to 16 letters, numbers, or underscores.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;First character must be a letter.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can&#39;t be a reserved word for the chosen database engine.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **masterUserPassword** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The password for the master user.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. The password for the master user is managed by the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can&#39;t be specified if &lt;code&gt;ManageMasterUserPassword&lt;/code&gt; is turned on.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can include any printable ASCII character except \&quot;/\&quot;, \&quot;\&quot;\&quot;, or \&quot;@\&quot;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Length Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for MariaDB - Must contain from 8 to 41 characters.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for Microsoft SQL Server - Must contain from 8 to 128 characters.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for MySQL - Must contain from 8 to 41 characters.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for Oracle - Must contain from 8 to 30 characters.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for PostgreSQL - Must contain from 8 to 128 characters.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **dbSecurityGroups** | [**List&lt;String&gt;**](String.md)| &lt;p&gt;A list of DB security groups to associate with this DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting applies to the legacy EC2-Classic platform, which is no longer used to create new DB instances. Use the &lt;code&gt;VpcSecurityGroupIds&lt;/code&gt; setting instead.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **vpcSecurityGroupIds** | [**List&lt;String&gt;**](String.md)| &lt;p&gt;A list of Amazon EC2 VPC security groups to associate with this DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. The associated list of EC2 VPC security groups is managed by the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: The default EC2 VPC security group for the DB subnet group&#39;s VPC.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **availabilityZone** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Availability Zone (AZ) where the database will be created. For information on Amazon Web Services Regions and Availability Zones, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.RegionsAndAvailabilityZones.html\&quot;&gt;Regions and Availability Zones&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For Amazon Aurora, each Aurora DB cluster hosts copies of its storage in three separate Availability Zones. Specify one of these Availability Zones. Aurora automatically chooses an appropriate Availability Zone if you don&#39;t specify one.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: A random, system-chosen Availability Zone in the endpoint&#39;s Amazon Web Services Region.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;The &lt;code&gt;AvailabilityZone&lt;/code&gt; parameter can&#39;t be specified if the DB instance is a Multi-AZ deployment.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;The specified Availability Zone must be in the same Amazon Web Services Region as the current endpoint.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Example: &lt;code&gt;us-east-1d&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **dbSubnetGroupName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;A DB subnet group to associate with this DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must match the name of an existing DB subnet group.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must not be &lt;code&gt;default&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Example: &lt;code&gt;mydbsubnetgroup&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **preferredMaintenanceWindow** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The time range each week during which system maintenance can occur. For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_UpgradeDBInstance.Maintenance.html#Concepts.DBMaintenance\&quot;&gt;Amazon RDS Maintenance Window&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The default is a 30-minute window selected at random from an 8-hour block of time for each Amazon Web Services Region, occurring on a random day of the week.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be in the format &lt;code&gt;ddd:hh24:mi-ddd:hh24:mi&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;The day values must be &lt;code&gt;mon | tue | wed | thu | fri | sat | sun&lt;/code&gt;. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be in Universal Coordinated Time (UTC).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must not conflict with the preferred backup window.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be at least 30 minutes.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **dbParameterGroupName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The name of the DB parameter group to associate with this DB instance. If you don&#39;t specify a value, then Amazon RDS uses the default DB parameter group for the specified DB engine and version.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be 1 to 255 letters, numbers, or hyphens.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;The first character must be a letter.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can&#39;t end with a hyphen or contain two consecutive hyphens.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **backupRetentionPeriod** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The number of days for which automated backups are retained. Setting this parameter to a positive number enables backups. Setting this parameter to &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt; disables automated backups.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. The retention period for automated backups is managed by the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;1&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be a value from 0 to 35.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can&#39;t be set to 0 if the DB instance is a source to read replicas.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can&#39;t be set to 0 for an RDS Custom for Oracle DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **preferredBackupWindow** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The daily time range during which automated backups are created if automated backups are enabled, using the &lt;code&gt;BackupRetentionPeriod&lt;/code&gt; parameter. The default is a 30-minute window selected at random from an 8-hour block of time for each Amazon Web Services Region. For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.html#USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.BackupWindow\&quot;&gt;Backup window&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. The daily time range for creating automated backups is managed by the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be in the format &lt;code&gt;hh24:mi-hh24:mi&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be in Universal Coordinated Time (UTC).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must not conflict with the preferred maintenance window.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be at least 30 minutes.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **port** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The port number on which the database accepts connections.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Aurora DB instances. The port number is managed by the cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values: &lt;code&gt;1150-65535&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for MariaDB - &lt;code&gt;3306&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for Microsoft SQL Server - &lt;code&gt;1433&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for MySQL - &lt;code&gt;3306&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for Oracle - &lt;code&gt;1521&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for PostgreSQL - &lt;code&gt;5432&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;For RDS for Microsoft SQL Server, the value can&#39;t be &lt;code&gt;1234&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;1434&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;3260&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;3343&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;3389&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;47001&lt;/code&gt;, or &lt;code&gt;49152-49156&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **multiAZ** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether the DB instance is a Multi-AZ deployment. You can&#39;t set the &lt;code&gt;AvailabilityZone&lt;/code&gt; parameter if the DB instance is a Multi-AZ deployment.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to the following DB instances:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Amazon Aurora (DB instance Availability Zones (AZs) are managed by the DB cluster.)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS Custom&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **engineVersion** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The version number of the database engine to use.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. The version number of the database engine the DB instance uses is managed by the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For a list of valid engine versions, use the &lt;code&gt;DescribeDBEngineVersions&lt;/code&gt; operation.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The following are the database engines and links to information about the major and minor versions that are available with Amazon RDS. Not every database engine is available for every Amazon Web Services Region.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;dl&gt; &lt;dt&gt;Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle&lt;/dt&gt; &lt;dd&gt; &lt;p&gt;A custom engine version (CEV) that you have previously created. This setting is required for RDS Custom for Oracle. The CEV name has the following format: 19.&lt;i&gt;customized_string&lt;/i&gt;. A valid CEV name is &lt;code&gt;19.my_cev1&lt;/code&gt;. For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/custom-creating.html#custom-creating.create\&quot;&gt; Creating an RDS Custom for Oracle DB instance&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/dd&gt; &lt;dt&gt;Amazon RDS Custom for SQL Server&lt;/dt&gt; &lt;dd&gt; &lt;p&gt;See &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/custom-reqs-limits-MS.html\&quot;&gt;RDS Custom for SQL Server general requirements&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/dd&gt; &lt;dt&gt;RDS for MariaDB&lt;/dt&gt; &lt;dd&gt; &lt;p&gt;For information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_MariaDB.html#MariaDB.Concepts.VersionMgmt\&quot;&gt;MariaDB on Amazon RDS versions&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/dd&gt; &lt;dt&gt;RDS for Microsoft SQL Server&lt;/dt&gt; &lt;dd&gt; &lt;p&gt;For information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_SQLServer.html#SQLServer.Concepts.General.VersionSupport\&quot;&gt;Microsoft SQL Server versions on Amazon RDS&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/dd&gt; &lt;dt&gt;RDS for MySQL&lt;/dt&gt; &lt;dd&gt; &lt;p&gt;For information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_MySQL.html#MySQL.Concepts.VersionMgmt\&quot;&gt;MySQL on Amazon RDS versions&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/dd&gt; &lt;dt&gt;RDS for Oracle&lt;/dt&gt; &lt;dd&gt; &lt;p&gt;For information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Appendix.Oracle.PatchComposition.html\&quot;&gt;Oracle Database Engine release notes&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/dd&gt; &lt;dt&gt;RDS for PostgreSQL&lt;/dt&gt; &lt;dd&gt; &lt;p&gt;For information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_PostgreSQL.html#PostgreSQL.Concepts\&quot;&gt;Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL versions and extensions&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/dd&gt; &lt;/dl&gt; | [optional] |
| **autoMinorVersionUpgrade** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether minor engine upgrades are applied automatically to the DB instance during the maintenance window. By default, minor engine upgrades are applied automatically.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you create an RDS Custom DB instance, you must set &lt;code&gt;AutoMinorVersionUpgrade&lt;/code&gt; to &lt;code&gt;false&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **licenseModel** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The license model information for this DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora or RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for MariaDB - &lt;code&gt;general-public-license&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for Microsoft SQL Server - &lt;code&gt;license-included&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for MySQL - &lt;code&gt;general-public-license&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for Oracle - &lt;code&gt;bring-your-own-license | license-included&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for PostgreSQL - &lt;code&gt;postgresql-license&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **iops** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The amount of Provisioned IOPS (input/output operations per second) to initially allocate for the DB instance. For information about valid IOPS values, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_Storage.html\&quot;&gt;Amazon RDS DB instance storage&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. Storage is managed by the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;For RDS for MariaDB, MySQL, Oracle, and PostgreSQL - Must be a multiple between .5 and 50 of the storage amount for the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;For RDS for SQL Server - Must be a multiple between 1 and 50 of the storage amount for the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **optionGroupName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The option group to associate the DB instance with.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Permanent options, such as the TDE option for Oracle Advanced Security TDE, can&#39;t be removed from an option group. Also, that option group can&#39;t be removed from a DB instance after it is associated with a DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora or RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **characterSetName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;For supported engines, the character set (&lt;code&gt;CharacterSet&lt;/code&gt;) to associate the DB instance with.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to the following DB instances:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Amazon Aurora - The character set is managed by the DB cluster. For more information, see &lt;code&gt;CreateDBCluster&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS Custom - However, if you need to change the character set, you can change it on the database itself.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **ncharCharacterSetName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The name of the NCHAR character set for the Oracle DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **publiclyAccessible** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether the DB instance is publicly accessible.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When the DB instance is publicly accessible, its Domain Name System (DNS) endpoint resolves to the private IP address from within the DB instance&#39;s virtual private cloud (VPC). It resolves to the public IP address from outside of the DB instance&#39;s VPC. Access to the DB instance is ultimately controlled by the security group it uses. That public access is not permitted if the security group assigned to the DB instance doesn&#39;t permit it.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When the DB instance isn&#39;t publicly accessible, it is an internal DB instance with a DNS name that resolves to a private IP address.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: The default behavior varies depending on whether &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroupName&lt;/code&gt; is specified.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroupName&lt;/code&gt; isn&#39;t specified, and &lt;code&gt;PubliclyAccessible&lt;/code&gt; isn&#39;t specified, the following applies:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the default VPC in the target Region doesn’t have an internet gateway attached to it, the DB instance is private.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the default VPC in the target Region has an internet gateway attached to it, the DB instance is public.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroupName&lt;/code&gt; is specified, and &lt;code&gt;PubliclyAccessible&lt;/code&gt; isn&#39;t specified, the following applies:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the subnets are part of a VPC that doesn’t have an internet gateway attached to it, the DB instance is private.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the subnets are part of a VPC that has an internet gateway attached to it, the DB instance is public.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **tags** | [**List&lt;Tag&gt;**](Tag.md)| Tags to assign to the DB instance. | [optional] |
| **dbClusterIdentifier** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The identifier of the DB cluster that this DB instance will belong to.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **storageType** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The storage type to associate with the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you specify &lt;code&gt;io1&lt;/code&gt; or &lt;code&gt;gp3&lt;/code&gt;, you must also include a value for the &lt;code&gt;Iops&lt;/code&gt; parameter.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. Storage is managed by the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values: &lt;code&gt;gp2 | gp3 | io1 | standard&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;io1&lt;/code&gt;, if the &lt;code&gt;Iops&lt;/code&gt; parameter is specified. Otherwise, &lt;code&gt;gp2&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **tdeCredentialArn** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The ARN from the key store with which to associate the instance for TDE encryption.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora or RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **tdeCredentialPassword** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The password for the given ARN from the key store in order to access the device.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **storageEncrypted** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifes whether the DB instance is encrypted. By default, it isn&#39;t encrypted.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For RDS Custom DB instances, either enable this setting or leave it unset. Otherwise, Amazon RDS reports an error.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. The encryption for DB instances is managed by the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **kmsKeyId** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier for an encrypted DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier is the key ARN, key ID, alias ARN, or alias name for the KMS key. To use a KMS key in a different Amazon Web Services account, specify the key ARN or alias ARN.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier is managed by the DB cluster. For more information, see &lt;code&gt;CreateDBCluster&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;StorageEncrypted&lt;/code&gt; is enabled, and you do not specify a value for the &lt;code&gt;KmsKeyId&lt;/code&gt; parameter, then Amazon RDS uses your default KMS key. There is a default KMS key for your Amazon Web Services account. Your Amazon Web Services account has a different default KMS key for each Amazon Web Services Region.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For Amazon RDS Custom, a KMS key is required for DB instances. For most RDS engines, if you leave this parameter empty while enabling &lt;code&gt;StorageEncrypted&lt;/code&gt;, the engine uses the default KMS key. However, RDS Custom doesn&#39;t use the default key when this parameter is empty. You must explicitly specify a key.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **domain** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Active Directory directory ID to create the DB instance in. Currently, only Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle, and PostgreSQL DB instances can be created in an Active Directory Domain.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/kerberos-authentication.html\&quot;&gt; Kerberos Authentication&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to the following DB instances:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Amazon Aurora (The domain is managed by the DB cluster.)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS Custom&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **domainFqdn** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of an Active Directory domain.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can&#39;t be longer than 64 characters.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Example: &lt;code&gt;mymanagedADtest.mymanagedAD.mydomain&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **domainOu** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Active Directory organizational unit for your DB instance to join.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be in the distinguished name format.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can&#39;t be longer than 64 characters.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Example: &lt;code&gt;OU&#x3D;mymanagedADtestOU,DC&#x3D;mymanagedADtest,DC&#x3D;mymanagedAD,DC&#x3D;mydomain&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **domainAuthSecretArn** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The ARN for the Secrets Manager secret with the credentials for the user joining the domain.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Example: &lt;code&gt;arn:aws:secretsmanager:region:account-number:secret:myselfmanagedADtestsecret-123456&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **domainDnsIps** | [**List&lt;String&gt;**](String.md)| &lt;p&gt;The IPv4 DNS IP addresses of your primary and secondary Active Directory domain controllers.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Two IP addresses must be provided. If there isn&#39;t a secondary domain controller, use the IP address of the primary domain controller for both entries in the list.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Example: &lt;code&gt;123.124.125.126,234.235.236.237&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **copyTagsToSnapshot** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to copy tags from the DB instance to snapshots of the DB instance. By default, tags are not copied.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. Copying tags to snapshots is managed by the DB cluster. Setting this value for an Aurora DB instance has no effect on the DB cluster setting.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **monitoringInterval** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The interval, in seconds, between points when Enhanced Monitoring metrics are collected for the DB instance. To disable collection of Enhanced Monitoring metrics, specify &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;MonitoringRoleArn&lt;/code&gt; is specified, then you must set &lt;code&gt;MonitoringInterval&lt;/code&gt; to a value other than &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values: &lt;code&gt;0 | 1 | 5 | 10 | 15 | 30 | 60&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **monitoringRoleArn** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The ARN for the IAM role that permits RDS to send enhanced monitoring metrics to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. For example, &lt;code&gt;arn:aws:iam:123456789012:role/emaccess&lt;/code&gt;. For information on creating a monitoring role, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_Monitoring.OS.html#USER_Monitoring.OS.Enabling\&quot;&gt;Setting Up and Enabling Enhanced Monitoring&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;MonitoringInterval&lt;/code&gt; is set to a value other than &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;, then you must supply a &lt;code&gt;MonitoringRoleArn&lt;/code&gt; value.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **domainIAMRoleName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The name of the IAM role to use when making API calls to the Directory Service.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to the following DB instances:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Amazon Aurora (The domain is managed by the DB cluster.)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS Custom&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **promotionTier** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The order of priority in which an Aurora Replica is promoted to the primary instance after a failure of the existing primary instance. For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.AuroraHighAvailability.html#Aurora.Managing.FaultTolerance\&quot;&gt; Fault Tolerance for an Aurora DB Cluster&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;1&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values: &lt;code&gt;0 - 15&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **timezone** | **String**| The time zone of the DB instance. The time zone parameter is currently supported only by &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_SQLServer.html#SQLServer.Concepts.General.TimeZone\&quot;&gt;Microsoft SQL Server&lt;/a&gt;. | [optional] |
| **enableIAMDatabaseAuthentication** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to enable mapping of Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management (IAM) accounts to database accounts. By default, mapping isn&#39;t enabled.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/UsingWithRDS.IAMDBAuth.html\&quot;&gt; IAM Database Authentication for MySQL and PostgreSQL&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to the following DB instances:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Amazon Aurora (Mapping Amazon Web Services IAM accounts to database accounts is managed by the DB cluster.)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS Custom&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **enablePerformanceInsights** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to enable Performance Insights for the DB instance. For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PerfInsights.html\&quot;&gt;Using Amazon Performance Insights&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **performanceInsightsKMSKeyId** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier for encryption of Performance Insights data.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier is the key ARN, key ID, alias ARN, or alias name for the KMS key.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you don&#39;t specify a value for &lt;code&gt;PerformanceInsightsKMSKeyId&lt;/code&gt;, then Amazon RDS uses your default KMS key. There is a default KMS key for your Amazon Web Services account. Your Amazon Web Services account has a different default KMS key for each Amazon Web Services Region.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **performanceInsightsRetentionPeriod** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The number of days to retain Performance Insights data.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;7&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;i&gt;month&lt;/i&gt; * 31, where &lt;i&gt;month&lt;/i&gt; is a number of months from 1-23. Examples: &lt;code&gt;93&lt;/code&gt; (3 months * 31), &lt;code&gt;341&lt;/code&gt; (11 months * 31), &lt;code&gt;589&lt;/code&gt; (19 months * 31)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;731&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;7&lt;/code&gt; days&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you specify a retention period that isn&#39;t valid, such as &lt;code&gt;94&lt;/code&gt;, Amazon RDS returns an error.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **enableCloudwatchLogsExports** | [**List&lt;String&gt;**](String.md)| &lt;p&gt;The list of log types that need to be enabled for exporting to CloudWatch Logs. For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_LogAccess.html#USER_LogAccess.Procedural.UploadtoCloudWatch\&quot;&gt; Publishing Database Logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to the following DB instances:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Amazon Aurora (CloudWatch Logs exports are managed by the DB cluster.)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS Custom&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;The following values are valid for each DB engine:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for MariaDB - &lt;code&gt;audit | error | general | slowquery&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for Microsoft SQL Server - &lt;code&gt;agent | error&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for MySQL - &lt;code&gt;audit | error | general | slowquery&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for Oracle - &lt;code&gt;alert | audit | listener | trace | oemagent&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for PostgreSQL - &lt;code&gt;postgresql | upgrade&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **processorFeatures** | [**List&lt;ProcessorFeature&gt;**](ProcessorFeature.md)| &lt;p&gt;The number of CPU cores and the number of threads per core for the DB instance class of the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora or RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **deletionProtection** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether the DB instance has deletion protection enabled. The database can&#39;t be deleted when deletion protection is enabled. By default, deletion protection isn&#39;t enabled. For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_DeleteInstance.html\&quot;&gt; Deleting a DB Instance&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. You can enable or disable deletion protection for the DB cluster. For more information, see &lt;code&gt;CreateDBCluster&lt;/code&gt;. DB instances in a DB cluster can be deleted even when deletion protection is enabled for the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **maxAllocatedStorage** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The upper limit in gibibytes (GiB) to which Amazon RDS can automatically scale the storage of the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information about this setting, including limitations that apply to it, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIOPS.StorageTypes.html#USER_PIOPS.Autoscaling\&quot;&gt; Managing capacity automatically with Amazon RDS storage autoscaling&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to the following DB instances:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Amazon Aurora (Storage is managed by the DB cluster.)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS Custom&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **enableCustomerOwnedIp** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to enable a customer-owned IP address (CoIP) for an RDS on Outposts DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;A &lt;i&gt;CoIP&lt;/i&gt; provides local or external connectivity to resources in your Outpost subnets through your on-premises network. For some use cases, a CoIP can provide lower latency for connections to the DB instance from outside of its virtual private cloud (VPC) on your local network.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information about RDS on Outposts, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-on-outposts.html\&quot;&gt;Working with Amazon RDS on Amazon Web Services Outposts&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information about CoIPs, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/outposts/latest/userguide/routing.html#ip-addressing\&quot;&gt;Customer-owned IP addresses&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Web Services Outposts User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **customIamInstanceProfile** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The instance profile associated with the underlying Amazon EC2 instance of an RDS Custom DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting is required for RDS Custom.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;The profile must exist in your account.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;The profile must have an IAM role that Amazon EC2 has permissions to assume.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;The instance profile name and the associated IAM role name must start with the prefix &lt;code&gt;AWSRDSCustom&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;For the list of permissions required for the IAM role, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/custom-setup-orcl.html#custom-setup-orcl.iam-vpc\&quot;&gt; Configure IAM and your VPC&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **backupTarget** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The location for storing automated backups and manual snapshots.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valie Values:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;outposts&lt;/code&gt; (Amazon Web Services Outposts)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;region&lt;/code&gt; (Amazon Web Services Region)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;region&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-on-outposts.html\&quot;&gt;Working with Amazon RDS on Amazon Web Services Outposts&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **networkType** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The network type of the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The network type is determined by the &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroup&lt;/code&gt; specified for the DB instance. A &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroup&lt;/code&gt; can support only the IPv4 protocol or the IPv4 and the IPv6 protocols (&lt;code&gt;DUAL&lt;/code&gt;).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_VPC.WorkingWithRDSInstanceinaVPC.html\&quot;&gt; Working with a DB instance in a VPC&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values: &lt;code&gt;IPV4 | DUAL&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **storageThroughput** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The storage throughput value for the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting applies only to the &lt;code&gt;gp3&lt;/code&gt; storage type.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora or RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **manageMasterUserPassword** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to manage the master user password with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html\&quot;&gt;Password management with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can&#39;t manage the master user password with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager if &lt;code&gt;MasterUserPassword&lt;/code&gt; is specified.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **masterUserSecretKmsKeyId** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier to encrypt a secret that is automatically generated and managed in Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting is valid only if the master user password is managed by RDS in Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager for the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier is the key ARN, key ID, alias ARN, or alias name for the KMS key. To use a KMS key in a different Amazon Web Services account, specify the key ARN or alias ARN.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you don&#39;t specify &lt;code&gt;MasterUserSecretKmsKeyId&lt;/code&gt;, then the &lt;code&gt;aws/secretsmanager&lt;/code&gt; KMS key is used to encrypt the secret. If the secret is in a different Amazon Web Services account, then you can&#39;t use the &lt;code&gt;aws/secretsmanager&lt;/code&gt; KMS key to encrypt the secret, and you must use a customer managed KMS key.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;There is a default KMS key for your Amazon Web Services account. Your Amazon Web Services account has a different default KMS key for each Amazon Web Services Region.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **caCertificateIdentifier** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The CA certificate identifier to use for the DB instance&#39;s server certificate.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/UsingWithRDS.SSL.html\&quot;&gt;Using SSL/TLS to encrypt a connection to a DB instance&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt; and &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/UsingWithRDS.SSL.html\&quot;&gt; Using SSL/TLS to encrypt a connection to a DB cluster&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **dbSystemId** | **String**| The Oracle system identifier (SID), which is the name of the Oracle database instance that manages your database files. In this context, the term \&quot;Oracle database instance\&quot; refers exclusively to the system global area (SGA) and Oracle background processes. If you don&#39;t specify a SID, the value defaults to &lt;code&gt;RDSCDB&lt;/code&gt;. The Oracle SID is also the name of your CDB. | [optional] |

### Return type

[**CreateDBInstanceResult**](CreateDBInstanceResult.md)

### Authorization

[hmac](../README.md#hmac)

### HTTP request headers

 - **Content-Type**: Not defined
 - **Accept**: text/xml

### HTTP response details
| Status code | Description | Response headers |
|-------------|-------------|------------------|
| **200** | Success |  -  |
| **480** | DBInstanceAlreadyExistsFault |  -  |
| **481** | InsufficientDBInstanceCapacityFault |  -  |
| **482** | DBParameterGroupNotFoundFault |  -  |
| **483** | DBSecurityGroupNotFoundFault |  -  |
| **484** | InstanceQuotaExceededFault |  -  |
| **485** | StorageQuotaExceededFault |  -  |
| **486** | DBSubnetGroupNotFoundFault |  -  |
| **487** | DBSubnetGroupDoesNotCoverEnoughAZs |  -  |
| **488** | InvalidDBClusterStateFault |  -  |
| **489** | InvalidSubnet |  -  |
| **490** | InvalidVPCNetworkStateFault |  -  |
| **491** | ProvisionedIopsNotAvailableInAZFault |  -  |
| **492** | OptionGroupNotFoundFault |  -  |
| **493** | DBClusterNotFoundFault |  -  |
| **494** | StorageTypeNotSupportedFault |  -  |
| **495** | AuthorizationNotFoundFault |  -  |
| **496** | KMSKeyNotAccessibleFault |  -  |
| **497** | DomainNotFoundFault |  -  |
| **498** | BackupPolicyNotFoundFault |  -  |
| **499** | NetworkTypeNotSupported |  -  |
| **500** | CertificateNotFoundFault |  -  |

<a id="gETCreateDBInstanceReadReplica"></a>
# **gETCreateDBInstanceReadReplica**
> CreateDBInstanceReadReplicaResult gETCreateDBInstanceReadReplica(dbInstanceIdentifier, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, sourceDBInstanceIdentifier, dbInstanceClass, availabilityZone, port, multiAZ, autoMinorVersionUpgrade, iops, optionGroupName, dbParameterGroupName, publiclyAccessible, tags, dbSubnetGroupName, vpcSecurityGroupIds, storageType, copyTagsToSnapshot, monitoringInterval, monitoringRoleArn, kmsKeyId, preSignedUrl, enableIAMDatabaseAuthentication, enablePerformanceInsights, performanceInsightsKMSKeyId, performanceInsightsRetentionPeriod, enableCloudwatchLogsExports, processorFeatures, useDefaultProcessorFeatures, deletionProtection, domain, domainIAMRoleName, domainFqdn, domainOu, domainAuthSecretArn, domainDnsIps, replicaMode, maxAllocatedStorage, customIamInstanceProfile, networkType, storageThroughput, enableCustomerOwnedIp, allocatedStorage, sourceDBClusterIdentifier, sourceRegion)



&lt;p&gt;Creates a new DB instance that acts as a read replica for an existing source DB instance or Multi-AZ DB cluster. You can create a read replica for a DB instance running MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle, PostgreSQL, or SQL Server. You can create a read replica for a Multi-AZ DB cluster running MySQL or PostgreSQL. For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html\&quot;&gt;Working with read replicas&lt;/a&gt; and &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/multi-az-db-clusters-concepts.html#multi-az-db-clusters-migrating-to-instance-with-read-replica\&quot;&gt;Migrating from a Multi-AZ DB cluster to a DB instance using a read replica&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Amazon Aurora doesn&#39;t support this operation. Call the &lt;code&gt;CreateDBInstance&lt;/code&gt; operation to create a DB instance for an Aurora DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;All read replica DB instances are created with backups disabled. All other attributes (including DB security groups and DB parameter groups) are inherited from the source DB instance or cluster, except as specified.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;important&gt; &lt;p&gt;Your source DB instance or cluster must have backup retention enabled.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/important&gt;

This doesn't apply to SQL Server or RDS Custom, which don't support cross-Region replicas.</p> </li> </ul>

    String kmsKeyId = "kmsKeyId_example"; // String | <p>The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier for an encrypted read replica.</p> <p>The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier is the key ARN, key ID, alias ARN, or alias name for the KMS key.</p> <p>If you create an encrypted read replica in the same Amazon Web Services Region as the source DB instance or Multi-AZ DB cluster, don't specify a value for this parameter.     String preSignedUrl = "preSignedUrl_example"; // String | <p>When you are creating a read replica from one Amazon Web Services GovCloud (US) Region to another or from one China Amazon Web Services Region to another, the URL that contains a Signature Version 4 signed request for the <code>CreateDBInstanceReadReplica</code> API operation in the source Amazon Web Services Region that contains the source DB instance.</p> <p>This setting applies only to Amazon Web Services GovCloud (US) Regions and China Amazon Web Services Regions. Source DB clusters aren't supported in Amazon Web Services GovCloud (US) Regions and China Amazon Web Services Regions.</p> <p>You must specify this parameter when you create an encrypted read replica from another Amazon Web Services Region by using the Amazon RDS API. Don't specify <code>PreSignedUrl</code> when you are creating an encrypted read replica in the same Amazon Web Services Region.</p> <p>The presigned URL must be a valid request for the <code>CreateDBInstanceReadReplica</code> API operation that can run in the source Amazon Web Services Region that contains the encrypted source DB instance. The presigned URL request must contain the following parameter values:</p> <ul> <li> <p> <code>DestinationRegion</code> - The Amazon Web Services Region that the encrypted read replica is created in. This Amazon Web Services Region is the same one where the <code>CreateDBInstanceReadReplica</code> operation is called that contains this presigned URL.</p> <p>For example, if you create an encrypted DB instance in the us-west-1 Amazon Web Services Region, from a source DB instance in the us-east-2 Amazon Web Services Region, then you call the <code>CreateDBInstanceReadReplica</code> operation in the us-east-1 Amazon Web Services Region and provide a presigned URL that contains a call to the <code>CreateDBInstanceReadReplica</code> operation in the us-west-2 Amazon Web Services Region. For this example, the <code>DestinationRegion</code> in the presigned URL must be set to the us-east-1 Amazon Web Services Region.</p> </li> <li> <p> <code>KmsKeyId</code> - The KMS key identifier for the key to use to encrypt the read replica in the destination Amazon Web Services Region. This is the same identifier for both the <code>CreateDBInstanceReadReplica</code> operation that is called in the destination Amazon Web Services Region, and the operation contained in the presigned URL.</p> </li> <li> <p> <code>SourceDBInstanceIdentifier</code> - The DB instance identifier for the encrypted DB instance to be replicated. This identifier must be in the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) format for the source Amazon Web Services Region. For example, if you are creating an encrypted read replica from a DB instance in the us-west-2 Amazon Web Services Region, then your <code>SourceDBInstanceIdentifier</code> looks like the following example: <code>arn:aws:rds:us-west-2:123456789012:instance:mysql-instance1-20161115</code>.</p> </li> </ul> <p>To learn how to generate a Signature Version 4 signed request, see <a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/sigv4-query-string-auth.html\">Authenticating Requests: Using Query Parameters (Amazon Web Services Signature Version 4)</a> and <a href=\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/signature-version-4.html\">Signature Version 4 Signing Process</a>.</p> <note> <p>If you are using an Amazon Web Services SDK tool or the CLI, you can specify <code>SourceRegion</code> (or <code>--source-region</code> for the CLI) instead of specifying <code>PreSignedUrl</code> manually. Specifying <code>SourceRegion</code> autogenerates a presigned URL that is a valid request for the operation that can run in the source Amazon Web Services Region.</p> <p> <code>SourceRegion</code> isn't supported for SQL Server, because Amazon RDS for SQL Server doesn't support cross-Region read replicas.</p> </note> <p>This setting doesn't apply to RDS Custom.</p><note><p>If you supply a value for this operation's <code>SourceRegion</code> parameter, a pre-signed URL will be calculated on your behalf.</p></note>

The main use case for mounted replicas is cross-Region disaster recovery. The primary database doesn't use Active Data Guard to transmit information to the mounted replica. If there isn&#39;t a secondary domain controller, use the IP address of the primary domain controller for both entries in the list.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Example: &lt;code&gt;123.124.125.126,234.235.236.237&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |

The main use case for mounted replicas is cross-Region disaster recovery. The primary database doesn&#39;t use Active Data Guard to transmit information to the mounted replica. Because it doesn&#39;t accept user connections, a mounted replica can&#39;t serve a read-only workload.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;You can create a combination of mounted and read-only DB replicas for the same primary DB instance. For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/oracle-read-replicas.html\&quot;&gt;Working with Oracle Read Replicas for Amazon RDS&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For RDS Custom, you must specify this parameter and set it to &lt;code&gt;mounted&lt;/code&gt;. <a id="gETCreateDBParameterGroup"></a>
# **gETCreateDBParameterGroup**
> CreateDBParameterGroupResult gETCreateDBParameterGroup(dbParameterGroupName, dbParameterGroupFamily, description, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, tags)



&lt;p&gt;Creates a new DB parameter group.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;A DB parameter group is initially created with the default parameters for the database engine used by the DB instance. To provide custom values for any of the parameters, you must modify the group after creating it using &lt;code&gt;ModifyDBParameterGroup&lt;/code&gt;. Once you&#39;ve created a DB parameter group, you need to associate it with your DB instance using &lt;code&gt;ModifyDBInstance&lt;/code&gt;. When you associate a new DB parameter group with a running DB instance, you need to reboot the DB instance without failover for the new DB parameter group and associated settings to take effect.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This command doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;important&gt; &lt;p&gt;After you create a DB parameter group, you should wait at least 5 minutes before creating your first DB instance that uses that DB parameter group as the default parameter group. This allows Amazon RDS to fully complete the create action before the parameter group is used as the default for a new DB instance. This is especially important for parameters that are critical when creating the default database for a DB instance, such as the character set for the default database defined by the &lt;code&gt;character_set_database&lt;/code&gt; parameter. You can use the &lt;i&gt;Parameter Groups&lt;/i&gt; option of the &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://console.aws.amazon.com/rds/\&quot;&gt;Amazon RDS console&lt;/a&gt; or the &lt;i&gt;DescribeDBParameters&lt;/i&gt; command to verify that your DB parameter group has been created or modified.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/important&gt;

# **gETCreateDBProxyEndpoint**
> CreateDBProxyEndpointResponse gETCreateDBProxyEndpoint(dbProxyName, dbProxyEndpointName, vpcSubnetIds, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, vpcSecurityGroupIds, targetRole, tags)



Creates a &lt;code&gt;DBProxyEndpoint&lt;/code&gt;. Only applies to proxies that are associated with Aurora DB clusters. You can use DB proxy endpoints to specify read/write or read-only access to the DB cluster. You can also use DB proxy endpoints to access a DB proxy through a different VPC than the proxy&#39;s default VPC.

For example, you can specify &lt;code&gt;SourceType&lt;/code&gt; &#x3D; &lt;code&gt;db-instance&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;SourceIds&lt;/code&gt; &#x3D; &lt;code&gt;mydbinstance1&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;mydbinstance2&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;EventCategories&lt;/code&gt; &#x3D; &lt;code&gt;Availability&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;Backup&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you specify both the &lt;code&gt;SourceType&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;SourceIds&lt;/code&gt;, such as &lt;code&gt;SourceType&lt;/code&gt; &#x3D; &lt;code&gt;db-instance&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;SourceIds&lt;/code&gt; &#x3D; &lt;code&gt;myDBInstance1&lt;/code&gt;, you are notified of all the &lt;code&gt;db-instance&lt;/code&gt; events for the specified source. # **gETCreateGlobalCluster**
> CreateGlobalClusterResult gETCreateGlobalCluster(action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, globalClusterIdentifier, sourceDBClusterIdentifier, engine, engineVersion, deletionProtection, databaseName, storageEncrypted)



&lt;p&gt;Creates an Aurora global database spread across multiple Amazon Web Services Regions. The global database contains a single primary cluster with read-write capability, and a read-only secondary cluster that receives data from the primary cluster through high-speed replication performed by the Aurora storage subsystem.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;You can create a global database that is initially empty, and then create the primary and secondary DB clusters in the global database. Or you can specify an existing Aurora cluster during the create operation, and this cluster becomes the primary cluster of the global database.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;This operation applies only to Aurora DB clusters.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/note&gt;

If it is, change the default before running this command.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;The CEV must not be associated with an RDS Custom DB instance, RDS Custom instance snapshot, or automated backup of your RDS Custom instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Typically, deletion takes a few minutes.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;The MediaImport service that imports files from Amazon S3 to create CEVs isn&#39;t integrated with Amazon Web Services CloudTrail. However, you might see calls from the API gateway that accesses your Amazon S3 bucket. # **gETDeleteDBCluster**
> DeleteDBClusterResult gETDeleteDBCluster(dbClusterIdentifier, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, skipFinalSnapshot, finalDBSnapshotIdentifier, deleteAutomatedBackups)

Manual DB cluster snapshots of the specified DB cluster are not deleted.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you&#39;re deleting a Multi-AZ DB cluster with read replicas, all cluster members are terminated and read replicas are promoted to standalone instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on Amazon Aurora, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html\&quot;&gt; What is Amazon Aurora?&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on Multi-AZ DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/multi-az-db-clusters-concepts.html\&quot;&gt; Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

<a id="gETDeleteDBInstance"></a>
# **gETDeleteDBInstance**
> DeleteDBInstanceResult gETDeleteDBInstance(dbInstanceIdentifier, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, skipFinalSnapshot, finalDBSnapshotIdentifier, deleteAutomatedBackups)



&lt;p&gt;The DeleteDBInstance action deletes a previously provisioned DB instance. When you delete a DB instance, all automated backups for that instance are deleted and can&#39;t be recovered. Manual DB snapshots of the DB instance to be deleted by &lt;code&gt;DeleteDBInstance&lt;/code&gt; are not deleted.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you request a final DB snapshot the status of the Amazon RDS DB instance is &lt;code&gt;deleting&lt;/code&gt; until the DB snapshot is created. The API action &lt;code&gt;DescribeDBInstance&lt;/code&gt; is used to monitor the status of this operation. The action can&#39;t be canceled or reverted once submitted.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When a DB instance is in a failure state and has a status of &lt;code&gt;failed&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;incompatible-restore&lt;/code&gt;, or &lt;code&gt;incompatible-network&lt;/code&gt;, you can only delete it when you skip creation of the final snapshot with the &lt;code&gt;SkipFinalSnapshot&lt;/code&gt; parameter.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the specified DB instance is part of an Amazon Aurora DB cluster, you can&#39;t delete the DB instance if both of the following conditions are true:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;The DB cluster is a read replica of another Amazon Aurora DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;The DB instance is the only instance in the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;To delete a DB instance in this case, first call the &lt;code&gt;PromoteReadReplicaDBCluster&lt;/code&gt; API action to promote the DB cluster so it&#39;s no longer a read replica. After the promotion completes, then call the &lt;code&gt;DeleteDBInstance&lt;/code&gt; API action to delete the final instance in the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt;

# **gETDescribeDBClusterSnapshotAttributes**
> DescribeDBClusterSnapshotAttributesResult gETDescribeDBClusterSnapshotAttributes(dbClusterSnapshotIdentifier, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders)



&lt;p&gt;Returns a list of DB cluster snapshot attribute names and values for a manual DB cluster snapshot.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When sharing snapshots with other Amazon Web Services accounts, &lt;code&gt;DescribeDBClusterSnapshotAttributes&lt;/code&gt; returns the &lt;code&gt;restore&lt;/code&gt; attribute and a list of IDs for the Amazon Web Services accounts that are authorized to copy or restore the manual DB cluster snapshot. If &lt;code&gt;all&lt;/code&gt; is included in the list of values for the &lt;code&gt;restore&lt;/code&gt; attribute, then the manual DB cluster snapshot is public and can be copied or restored by all Amazon Web Services accounts.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;To add or remove access for an Amazon Web Services account to copy or restore a manual DB cluster snapshot, or to make the manual DB cluster snapshot public or private, use the &lt;code&gt;ModifyDBClusterSnapshotAttribute&lt;/code&gt; API action.&lt;/p&gt;

<a id="gETDescribeEvents"></a>
# **gETDescribeEvents**
> EventsMessage gETDescribeEvents(action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, sourceIdentifier, sourceType, startTime, endTime, duration, eventCategories, filters, maxRecords, marker)



&lt;p&gt;Returns events related to DB instances, DB clusters, DB parameter groups, DB security groups, DB snapshots, DB cluster snapshots, and RDS Proxies for the past 14 days. Events specific to a particular DB instance, DB cluster, DB parameter group, DB security group, DB snapshot, DB cluster snapshot group, or RDS Proxy can be obtained by providing the name as a parameter.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on working with events, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/working-with-events.html\&quot;&gt;Monitoring Amazon RDS events&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt; and &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/working-with-events.html\&quot;&gt;Monitoring Amazon Aurora events&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;By default, RDS returns events that were generated in the past hour.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/note&gt;

<a id="gETFailoverDBCluster"></a>
# **gETFailoverDBCluster**
> FailoverDBClusterResult gETFailoverDBCluster(dbClusterIdentifier, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, targetDBInstanceIdentifier)



&lt;p&gt;Forces a failover for a DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For an Aurora DB cluster, failover for a DB cluster promotes one of the Aurora Replicas (read-only instances) in the DB cluster to be the primary DB instance (the cluster writer).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For a Multi-AZ DB cluster, failover for a DB cluster promotes one of the readable standby DB instances (read-only instances) in the DB cluster to be the primary DB instance (the cluster writer).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;An Amazon Aurora DB cluster automatically fails over to an Aurora Replica, if one exists, when the primary DB instance fails. A Multi-AZ DB cluster automatically fails over to a readable standby DB instance when the primary DB instance fails.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;To simulate a failure of a primary instance for testing, you can force a failover. Because each instance in a DB cluster has its own endpoint address, make sure to clean up and re-establish any existing connections that use those endpoint addresses when the failover is complete.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on Amazon Aurora DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html\&quot;&gt; What is Amazon Aurora?&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on Multi-AZ DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/multi-az-db-clusters-concepts.html\&quot;&gt; Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

<a id="gETFailoverGlobalCluster"></a>
# **gETFailoverGlobalCluster**
> FailoverGlobalClusterResult gETFailoverGlobalCluster(globalClusterIdentifier, targetDbClusterIdentifier, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders)



&lt;p&gt;Initiates the failover process for an Aurora global database (&lt;a&gt;GlobalCluster&lt;/a&gt;).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;A failover for an Aurora global database promotes one of secondary read-only DB clusters to be the primary DB cluster and demotes the primary DB cluster to being a secondary (read-only) DB cluster. In other words, the role of the current primary DB cluster and the selected (target) DB cluster are switched. The selected secondary DB cluster assumes full read/write capabilities for the Aurora global database.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information about failing over an Amazon Aurora global database, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database-disaster-recovery.html#aurora-global-database-disaster-recovery.managed-failover\&quot;&gt;Managed planned failover for Amazon Aurora global databases&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;This action applies to &lt;a&gt;GlobalCluster&lt;/a&gt; (Aurora global databases) only. Use this action only on healthy Aurora global databases with running Aurora DB clusters and no Region-wide outages, to test disaster recovery scenarios or to reconfigure your Aurora global database topology.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/note&gt;

# **gETModifyActivityStream**
> ModifyActivityStreamResponse gETModifyActivityStream(action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, resourceArn, auditPolicyState)



&lt;p&gt;Changes the audit policy state of a database activity stream to either locked (default) or unlocked. A locked policy is read-only, whereas an unlocked policy is read/write. If your activity stream is started and locked, you can unlock it, customize your audit policy, and then lock your activity stream. Restarting the activity stream isn&#39;t required. For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/DBActivityStreams.Modifying.html\&quot;&gt; Modifying a database activity stream&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This operation is supported for RDS for Oracle and Microsoft SQL Server.&lt;/p&gt;

# **gETModifyCurrentDBClusterCapacity**
> DBClusterCapacityInfo gETModifyCurrentDBClusterCapacity(dbClusterIdentifier, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, capacity, secondsBeforeTimeout, timeoutAction)



&lt;p&gt;Set the capacity of an Aurora Serverless v1 DB cluster to a specific value.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Aurora Serverless v1 scales seamlessly based on the workload on the DB cluster. In some cases, the capacity might not scale fast enough to meet a sudden change in workload, such as a large number of new transactions. Call &lt;code&gt;ModifyCurrentDBClusterCapacity&lt;/code&gt; to set the capacity explicitly.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;After this call sets the DB cluster capacity, Aurora Serverless v1 can automatically scale the DB cluster based on the cooldown period for scaling up and the cooldown period for scaling down.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information about Aurora Serverless v1, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless.html\&quot;&gt;Using Amazon Aurora Serverless v1&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;important&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you call &lt;code&gt;ModifyCurrentDBClusterCapacity&lt;/code&gt; with the default &lt;code&gt;TimeoutAction&lt;/code&gt;, connections that prevent Aurora Serverless v1 from finding a scaling point might be dropped. For more information about scaling points, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless.how-it-works.html#aurora-serverless.how-it-works.auto-scaling\&quot;&gt; Autoscaling for Aurora Serverless v1&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/important&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;This action only applies to Aurora Serverless v1 DB clusters.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/note&gt;
