| **storageType** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The storage type to associate with the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For information on storage types for Aurora DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Overview.StorageReliability.html#aurora-storage-type\&quot;&gt;Storage configurations for Amazon Aurora DB clusters&lt;/a&gt;. For information on storage types for Multi-AZ DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/create-multi-az-db-cluster.html#create-multi-az-db-cluster-settings\&quot;&gt;Settings for creating Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When specified for a Multi-AZ DB cluster, a value for the &lt;code&gt;Iops&lt;/code&gt; parameter is required.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Aurora DB clusters - &lt;code&gt;aurora | aurora-iopt1&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Multi-AZ DB clusters - &lt;code&gt;io1&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Aurora DB clusters - &lt;code&gt;aurora&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Multi-AZ DB clusters - &lt;code&gt;io1&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **iops** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The amount of Provisioned IOPS (input/output operations per second) to be initially allocated for each DB instance in the Multi-AZ DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For information about valid IOPS values, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_Storage.html#USER_PIOPS\&quot;&gt;Amazon RDS Provisioned IOPS storage&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be a multiple between .5 and 50 of the storage amount for the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **autoMinorVersionUpgrade** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether minor engine upgrades are applied automatically to the DB cluster during the maintenance window. By default, minor engine upgrades are applied automatically.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **monitoringInterval** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The interval, in seconds, between points when Enhanced Monitoring metrics are collected for the DB cluster. To turn off collecting Enhanced Monitoring metrics, specify &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;MonitoringRoleArn&lt;/code&gt; is specified, also set &lt;code&gt;MonitoringInterval&lt;/code&gt; to a value other than &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values: &lt;code&gt;0 | 1 | 5 | 10 | 15 | 30 | 60&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **monitoringRoleArn** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the IAM role that permits RDS to send Enhanced Monitoring metrics to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. An example is &lt;code&gt;arn:aws:iam:123456789012:role/emaccess&lt;/code&gt;. For information on creating a monitoring role, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_Monitoring.html#USER_Monitoring.OS.IAMRole\&quot;&gt;To create an IAM role for Amazon RDS Enhanced Monitoring&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;MonitoringInterval&lt;/code&gt; is set to a value other than &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;, supply a &lt;code&gt;MonitoringRoleArn&lt;/code&gt; value.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **enablePerformanceInsights** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to turn on Performance Insights for the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PerfInsights.html\&quot;&gt; Using Amazon Performance Insights&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **performanceInsightsKMSKeyId** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier for encryption of Performance Insights data.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier is the key ARN, key ID, alias ARN, or alias name for the KMS key.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you don&#39;t specify a value for &lt;code&gt;PerformanceInsightsKMSKeyId&lt;/code&gt;, then Amazon RDS uses your default KMS key. There is a default KMS key for your Amazon Web Services account. Your Amazon Web Services account has a different default KMS key for each Amazon Web Services Region.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **performanceInsightsRetentionPeriod** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The number of days to retain Performance Insights data.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;7&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;i&gt;month&lt;/i&gt; * 31, where &lt;i&gt;month&lt;/i&gt; is a number of months from 1-23. Examples: &lt;code&gt;93&lt;/code&gt; (3 months * 31), &lt;code&gt;341&lt;/code&gt; (11 months * 31), &lt;code&gt;589&lt;/code&gt; (19 months * 31)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;731&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;7&lt;/code&gt; days&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you specify a retention period that isn&#39;t valid, such as &lt;code&gt;94&lt;/code&gt;, Amazon RDS issues an error.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **serverlessV2ScalingConfiguration** | [**GETCreateDBClusterServerlessV2ScalingConfigurationParameter**](.md)|  | [optional] |
| **networkType** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The network type of the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The network type is determined by the &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroup&lt;/code&gt; specified for the DB cluster. A &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroup&lt;/code&gt; can support only the IPv4 protocol or the IPv4 and the IPv6 protocols (&lt;code&gt;DUAL&lt;/code&gt;).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/USER_VPC.WorkingWithRDSInstanceinaVPC.html\&quot;&gt; Working with a DB instance in a VPC&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values: &lt;code&gt;IPV4 | DUAL&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **manageMasterUserPassword** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to manage the master user password with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the DB cluster doesn&#39;t manage the master user password with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager, you can turn on this management. In this case, you can&#39;t specify &lt;code&gt;MasterUserPassword&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the DB cluster already manages the master user password with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager, and you specify that the master user password is not managed with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager, then you must specify &lt;code&gt;MasterUserPassword&lt;/code&gt;. In this case, RDS deletes the secret and uses the new password for the master user specified by &lt;code&gt;MasterUserPassword&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html\&quot;&gt;Password management with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt; and &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html\&quot;&gt;Password management with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **rotateMasterUserPassword** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to rotate the secret managed by Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager for the master user password.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting is valid only if the master user password is managed by RDS in Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager for the DB cluster. The secret value contains the updated password.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html\&quot;&gt;Password management with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt; and &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html\&quot;&gt;Password management with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;You must apply the change immediately when rotating the master user password.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **masterUserSecretKmsKeyId** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier to encrypt a secret that is automatically generated and managed in Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting is valid only if both of the following conditions are met:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;The DB cluster doesn&#39;t manage the master user password in Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the DB cluster already manages the master user password in Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager, you can&#39;t change the KMS key that is used to encrypt the secret.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;You are turning on &lt;code&gt;ManageMasterUserPassword&lt;/code&gt; to manage the master user password in Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you are turning on &lt;code&gt;ManageMasterUserPassword&lt;/code&gt; and don&#39;t specify &lt;code&gt;MasterUserSecretKmsKeyId&lt;/code&gt;, then the &lt;code&gt;aws/secretsmanager&lt;/code&gt; KMS key is used to encrypt the secret. If the secret is in a different Amazon Web Services account, then you can&#39;t use the &lt;code&gt;aws/secretsmanager&lt;/code&gt; KMS key to encrypt the secret, and you must use a customer managed KMS key.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier is the key ARN, key ID, alias ARN, or alias name for the KMS key. To use a KMS key in a different Amazon Web Services account, specify the key ARN or alias ARN.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;There is a default KMS key for your Amazon Web Services account. Your Amazon Web Services account has a different default KMS key for each Amazon Web Services Region.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **engineMode** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The DB engine mode of the DB cluster, either &lt;code&gt;provisioned&lt;/code&gt; or &lt;code&gt;serverless&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;The DB engine mode can be modified only from &lt;code&gt;serverless&lt;/code&gt; to &lt;code&gt;provisioned&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/note&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/APIReference/API_CreateDBCluster.html\&quot;&gt; CreateDBCluster&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **allowEngineModeChange** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether engine mode changes from &lt;code&gt;serverless&lt;/code&gt; to &lt;code&gt;provisioned&lt;/code&gt; are allowed.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for Cluster Type: Aurora Serverless v1 DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;You must allow engine mode changes when specifying a different value for the &lt;code&gt;EngineMode&lt;/code&gt; parameter from the DB cluster&#39;s current engine mode.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **enableLocalWriteForwarding** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether read replicas can forward write operations to the writer DB instance in the DB cluster. By default, write operations aren&#39;t allowed on reader DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |

<a id="gETModifyDBClusterParameterGroup"></a>
# **gETModifyDBClusterParameterGroup**
> DBClusterParameterGroupNameMessage gETModifyDBClusterParameterGroup(dbClusterParameterGroupName, parameters, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders)



&lt;p&gt;Modifies the parameters of a DB cluster parameter group. To modify more than one parameter, submit a list of the following: &lt;code&gt;ParameterName&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;ParameterValue&lt;/code&gt;, and &lt;code&gt;ApplyMethod&lt;/code&gt;. A maximum of 20 parameters can be modified in a single request.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;important&gt; &lt;p&gt;After you create a DB cluster parameter group, you should wait at least 5 minutes before creating your first DB cluster that uses that DB cluster parameter group as the default parameter group. This allows Amazon RDS to fully complete the create action before the parameter group is used as the default for a new DB cluster. This is especially important for parameters that are critical when creating the default database for a DB cluster, such as the character set for the default database defined by the &lt;code&gt;character_set_database&lt;/code&gt; parameter. You can use the &lt;i&gt;Parameter Groups&lt;/i&gt; option of the &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://console.aws.amazon.com/rds/\&quot;&gt;Amazon RDS console&lt;/a&gt; or the &lt;code&gt;DescribeDBClusterParameters&lt;/code&gt; operation to verify that your DB cluster parameter group has been created or modified.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the modified DB cluster parameter group is used by an Aurora Serverless v1 cluster, Aurora applies the update immediately. The cluster restart might interrupt your workload. In that case, your application must reopen any connections and retry any transactions that were active when the parameter changes took effect.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/important&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on Amazon Aurora DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html\&quot;&gt; What is Amazon Aurora?&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on Multi-AZ DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/multi-az-db-clusters-concepts.html\&quot;&gt; Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt;

### Example
```java
// Import classes:
import org.openapitools.client.ApiClient;
import org.openapitools.client.ApiException;

public class Example {
  public static void main(String[] args) {
    ApiClient defaultClient = Configuration.getDefaultApiClient();
    defaultClient.setBasePath("http://rds.us-east-1.amazonaws.com");
    
    // Configure API key authorization: hmac
    ApiKeyAuth hmac = (ApiKeyAuth) defaultClient.getAuthentication("hmac");
    hmac.setApiKey("YOUR API KEY");
    // Uncomment the following line to set a prefix for the API key, e.g. "Token" (defaults to null)
    //hmac.setApiKeyPrefix("Token");

    DefaultApi apiInstance = new DefaultApi(defaultClient);
    String dbClusterParameterGroupName = "dbClusterParameterGroupName_example"; // String | The name of the DB cluster parameter group to modify.
    List<Parameter> parameters = Arrays.asList(); // List<Parameter> | <p>A list of parameters in the DB cluster parameter group to modify.</p> <p>Valid Values (for the application method): <code>immediate | pending-reboot</code> </p> <note> <p>You can use the <code>immediate</code> value with dynamic parameters only. You can use the <code>pending-reboot</code> value for both dynamic and static parameters.</p> <p>When the application method is <code>immediate</code>, changes to dynamic parameters are applied immediately to the DB clusters associated with the parameter group. When the application method is <code>pending-reboot</code>, changes to dynamic and static parameters are applied after a reboot without failover to the DB clusters associated with the parameter group.</p> </note>
    String action = "ModifyDBClusterParameterGroup"; // String | 
    String version = "2014-10-31"; // String | 
    String xAmzContentSha256 = "xAmzContentSha256_example"; // String |
```

# **gETModifyDBClusterSnapshotAttribute**
> ModifyDBClusterSnapshotAttributeResult gETModifyDBClusterSnapshotAttribute(dbClusterSnapshotIdentifier, attributeName, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, valuesToAdd, valuesToRemove)



&lt;p&gt;Adds an attribute and values to, or removes an attribute and values from, a manual DB cluster snapshot.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;To share a manual DB cluster snapshot with other Amazon Web Services accounts, specify &lt;code&gt;restore&lt;/code&gt; as the &lt;code&gt;AttributeName&lt;/code&gt; and use the &lt;code&gt;ValuesToAdd&lt;/code&gt; parameter to add a list of IDs of the Amazon Web Services accounts that are authorized to restore the manual DB cluster snapshot. Use the value &lt;code&gt;all&lt;/code&gt; to make the manual DB cluster snapshot public, which means that it can be copied or restored by all Amazon Web Services accounts.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;Don&#39;t add the &lt;code&gt;all&lt;/code&gt; value for any manual DB cluster snapshots that contain private information that you don&#39;t want available to all Amazon Web Services accounts.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/note&gt; &lt;p&gt;If a manual DB cluster snapshot is encrypted, it can be shared, but only by specifying a list of authorized Amazon Web Services account IDs for the &lt;code&gt;ValuesToAdd&lt;/code&gt; parameter. You can&#39;t use &lt;code&gt;all&lt;/code&gt; as a value for that parameter in this case.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;To view which Amazon Web Services accounts have access to copy or restore a manual DB cluster snapshot, or whether a manual DB cluster snapshot is public or private, use the &lt;a&gt;DescribeDBClusterSnapshotAttributes&lt;/a&gt; API operation. The accounts are returned as values for the &lt;code&gt;restore&lt;/code&gt; attribute.&lt;/p&gt;

Changing this parameter doesn't result in an outage and the change is asynchronously applied as soon as possible.</p> <p>This setting doesn't apply to RDS Custom DB instances.</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Major version upgrades must be allowed when specifying a value for the <code>EngineVersion</code> parameter that's a different major version than the DB instance's current version.</p> </li> </ul>
```java
    Boolean autoMinorVersionUpgrade = true; // Boolean | <p>Specifies whether minor version upgrades are applied automatically to the DB instance during the maintenance window.     String licenseModel = "licenseModel_example"; // String | <p>The license model for the DB instance.</p> <p>This setting doesn't apply to Amazon Aurora or RDS Custom DB instances.</p> <p>Valid Values:</p> <ul> <li> <p>RDS for MariaDB - <code>general-public-license</code> </p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for Microsoft SQL Server - <code>license-included</code> </p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for MySQL - <code>general-public-license</code> </p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for Oracle - <code>bring-your-own-license | license-included</code> </p> </li> <li> <p>RDS for PostgreSQL - <code>postgresql-license</code> </p> </li> </ul>
    Integer iops = 56; // Integer | <p>The new Provisioned IOPS (I/O operations per second) value for the RDS instance.</p> <p>Changing this setting doesn't result in an outage and the change is applied during the next maintenance window unless the <code>ApplyImmediately</code> parameter is enabled for this request. The DB instance will require a reboot for the change in storage type to take effect.</p> <p>If you choose to migrate your DB instance from using standard storage to using Provisioned IOPS, or from using Provisioned IOPS to using standard storage, the process can take time. The duration of the migration depends on several factors such as database load, storage size, storage type (standard or Provisioned IOPS), amount of IOPS provisioned (if any), and the number of prior scale storage operations. Typical migration times are under 24 hours, but the process can take up to several days in some cases. During the migration, the DB instance is available for use, but might experience performance degradation. While the migration takes place, nightly backups for the instance are suspended. No other Amazon RDS operations can take place for the instance, including modifying the instance, rebooting the instance, deleting the instance, creating a read replica for the instance, and creating a DB snapshot of the instance.</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>For RDS for MariaDB, RDS for MySQL, RDS for Oracle, and RDS for PostgreSQL - The value supplied must be at least 10% greater than the current value.     String storageType = "storageType_example"; // String | <p>The storage type to associate with the DB instance.</p> <p>If you specify Provisioned IOPS (<code>io1</code>), you must also include a value for the <code>Iops</code> parameter.</p> <p>If you choose to migrate your DB instance from using standard storage to using Provisioned IOPS, or from using Provisioned IOPS to using standard storage, the process can take time. Typical migration times are under 24 hours, but the process can take up to several days in some cases. During the migration, the DB instance is available for use, but might experience performance degradation. While the migration takes place, nightly backups for the instance are suspended. No other Amazon RDS operations can take place for the instance, including modifying the instance, rebooting the instance, deleting the instance, creating a read replica for the instance, and creating a DB snapshot of the instance.</p> <p>Valid Values: <code>gp2 | gp3 | io1 | standard</code> </p> <p>Default: <code>io1</code>, if the <code>Iops</code> parameter is specified.     String domainFqdn = "domainFqdn_example"; // String | <p>The fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of an Active Directory domain.</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Can't be longer than 64 characters.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Example: <code>mymanagedADtest.mymanagedAD.mydomain</code> </p>

    Boolean publiclyAccessible = true; // Boolean | <p>Specifies whether the DB instance is publicly accessible.</p> <p>When the DB cluster is publicly accessible, its Domain Name System (DNS) endpoint resolves to the private IP address from within the DB cluster's virtual private cloud (VPC).     String replicaMode = "open-read-only"; // String | <p>A value that sets the open mode of a replica database to either mounted or read-only.</p> <note> <p>Currently, this parameter is only supported for Oracle DB instances.</p> </note> <p>Mounted DB replicas are included in Oracle Enterprise Edition. Otherwise, &lt;code&gt;gp2&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
```
| **tdeCredentialArn** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The ARN from the key store with which to associate the instance for TDE encryption.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **tdeCredentialPassword** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The password for the given ARN from the key store in order to access the device.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **caCertificateIdentifier** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The CA certificate identifier to use for the DB instance&#39;s server certificate.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/UsingWithRDS.SSL.html\&quot;&gt;Using SSL/TLS to encrypt a connection to a DB instance&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt; and &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/UsingWithRDS.SSL.html\&quot;&gt; Using SSL/TLS to encrypt a connection to a DB cluster&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **domain** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Active Directory directory ID to move the DB instance to. Specify &lt;code&gt;none&lt;/code&gt; to remove the instance from its current domain. You must create the domain before this operation. Currently, you can create only MySQL, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle, and PostgreSQL DB instances in an Active Directory Domain.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/kerberos-authentication.html\&quot;&gt; Kerberos Authentication&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **domainFqdn** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of an Active Directory domain.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can&#39;t be longer than 64 characters.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Example: &lt;code&gt;mymanagedADtest.mymanagedAD.mydomain&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **domainOu** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Active Directory organizational unit for your DB instance to join.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be in the distinguished name format.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can&#39;t be longer than 64 characters.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Example: &lt;code&gt;OU&#x3D;mymanagedADtestOU,DC&#x3D;mymanagedADtest,DC&#x3D;mymanagedAD,DC&#x3D;mydomain&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **domainAuthSecretArn** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The ARN for the Secrets Manager secret with the credentials for the user joining the domain.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Example: &lt;code&gt;arn:aws:secretsmanager:region:account-number:secret:myselfmanagedADtestsecret-123456&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **domainDnsIps** | [**List&lt;String&gt;**](String.md)| &lt;p&gt;The IPv4 DNS IP addresses of your primary and secondary Active Directory domain controllers.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Two IP addresses must be provided. If there isn&#39;t a secondary domain controller, use the IP address of the primary domain controller for both entries in the list.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Example: &lt;code&gt;123.124.125.126,234.235.236.237&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **copyTagsToSnapshot** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to copy all tags from the DB instance to snapshots of the DB instance. By default, tags aren&#39;t copied.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora DB instances. Copying tags to snapshots is managed by the DB cluster. Setting this value for an Aurora DB instance has no effect on the DB cluster setting. For more information, see &lt;code&gt;ModifyDBCluster&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **monitoringInterval** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The interval, in seconds, between points when Enhanced Monitoring metrics are collected for the DB instance. To disable collection of Enhanced Monitoring metrics, specify &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;MonitoringRoleArn&lt;/code&gt; is specified, set &lt;code&gt;MonitoringInterval&lt;/code&gt; to a value other than &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values: &lt;code&gt;0 | 1 | 5 | 10 | 15 | 30 | 60&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **dbPortNumber** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The port number on which the database accepts connections.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The value of the &lt;code&gt;DBPortNumber&lt;/code&gt; parameter must not match any of the port values specified for options in the option group for the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you change the &lt;code&gt;DBPortNumber&lt;/code&gt; value, your database restarts regardless of the value of the &lt;code&gt;ApplyImmediately&lt;/code&gt; parameter.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values: &lt;code&gt;1150-65535&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Amazon Aurora - &lt;code&gt;3306&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for MariaDB - &lt;code&gt;3306&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for Microsoft SQL Server - &lt;code&gt;1433&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for MySQL - &lt;code&gt;3306&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for Oracle - &lt;code&gt;1521&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;RDS for PostgreSQL - &lt;code&gt;5432&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;For RDS for Microsoft SQL Server, the value can&#39;t be &lt;code&gt;1234&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;1434&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;3260&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;3343&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;3389&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;47001&lt;/code&gt;, or &lt;code&gt;49152-49156&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **publiclyAccessible** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether the DB instance is publicly accessible.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When the DB cluster is publicly accessible, its Domain Name System (DNS) endpoint resolves to the private IP address from within the DB cluster&#39;s virtual private cloud (VPC). It resolves to the public IP address from outside of the DB cluster&#39;s VPC. Access to the DB cluster is ultimately controlled by the security group it uses. That public access isn&#39;t permitted if the security group assigned to the DB cluster doesn&#39;t permit it.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When the DB instance isn&#39;t publicly accessible, it is an internal DB instance with a DNS name that resolves to a private IP address.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;PubliclyAccessible&lt;/code&gt; only applies to DB instances in a VPC. The DB instance must be part of a public subnet and &lt;code&gt;PubliclyAccessible&lt;/code&gt; must be enabled for it to be publicly accessible.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Changes to the &lt;code&gt;PubliclyAccessible&lt;/code&gt; parameter are applied immediately regardless of the value of the &lt;code&gt;ApplyImmediately&lt;/code&gt; parameter.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **monitoringRoleArn** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The ARN for the IAM role that permits RDS to send enhanced monitoring metrics to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. For example, &lt;code&gt;arn:aws:iam:123456789012:role/emaccess&lt;/code&gt;. For information on creating a monitoring role, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_Monitoring.html#USER_Monitoring.OS.IAMRole\&quot;&gt;To create an IAM role for Amazon RDS Enhanced Monitoring&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;MonitoringInterval&lt;/code&gt; is set to a value other than &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;, supply a &lt;code&gt;MonitoringRoleArn&lt;/code&gt; value.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **domainIAMRoleName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The name of the IAM role to use when making API calls to the Directory Service.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **disableDomain** | **Boolean**| Specifies whether to remove the DB instance from the Active Directory domain. | [optional] |
| **promotionTier** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The order of priority in which an Aurora Replica is promoted to the primary instance after a failure of the existing primary instance. For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.AuroraHighAvailability.html#Aurora.Managing.FaultTolerance\&quot;&gt; Fault Tolerance for an Aurora DB Cluster&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;1&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values: &lt;code&gt;0 - 15&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **enableIAMDatabaseAuthentication** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to enable mapping of Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management (IAM) accounts to database accounts. By default, mapping isn&#39;t enabled.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora. Mapping Amazon Web Services IAM accounts to database accounts is managed by the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information about IAM database authentication, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/UsingWithRDS.IAMDBAuth.html\&quot;&gt; IAM Database Authentication for MySQL and PostgreSQL&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **enablePerformanceInsights** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to enable Performance Insights for the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PerfInsights.html\&quot;&gt;Using Amazon Performance Insights&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **performanceInsightsKMSKeyId** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier for encryption of Performance Insights data.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier is the key ARN, key ID, alias ARN, or alias name for the KMS key.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you don&#39;t specify a value for &lt;code&gt;PerformanceInsightsKMSKeyId&lt;/code&gt;, then Amazon RDS uses your default KMS key. There is a default KMS key for your Amazon Web Services account. Your Amazon Web Services account has a different default KMS key for each Amazon Web Services Region.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **performanceInsightsRetentionPeriod** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The number of days to retain Performance Insights data.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;7&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;i&gt;month&lt;/i&gt; * 31, where &lt;i&gt;month&lt;/i&gt; is a number of months from 1-23. Examples: &lt;code&gt;93&lt;/code&gt; (3 months * 31), &lt;code&gt;341&lt;/code&gt; (11 months * 31), &lt;code&gt;589&lt;/code&gt; (19 months * 31)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;731&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;7&lt;/code&gt; days&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you specify a retention period that isn&#39;t valid, such as &lt;code&gt;94&lt;/code&gt;, Amazon RDS returns an error.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **cloudwatchLogsExportConfiguration** | [**GETModifyDBClusterCloudwatchLogsExportConfigurationParameter**](.md)| &lt;p&gt;The log types to be enabled for export to CloudWatch Logs for a specific DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;A change to the &lt;code&gt;CloudwatchLogsExportConfiguration&lt;/code&gt; parameter is always applied to the DB instance immediately. Therefore, the &lt;code&gt;ApplyImmediately&lt;/code&gt; parameter has no effect.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **processorFeatures** | [**List&lt;ProcessorFeature&gt;**](ProcessorFeature.md)| &lt;p&gt;The number of CPU cores and the number of threads per core for the DB instance class of the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **useDefaultProcessorFeatures** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether the DB instance class of the DB instance uses its default processor features.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **deletionProtection** | **Boolean**| Specifies whether the DB instance has deletion protection enabled. The database can&#39;t be deleted when deletion protection is enabled. By default, deletion protection isn&#39;t enabled. For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_DeleteInstance.html\&quot;&gt; Deleting a DB Instance&lt;/a&gt;. | [optional] |
| **maxAllocatedStorage** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The upper limit in gibibytes (GiB) to which Amazon RDS can automatically scale the storage of the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information about this setting, including limitations that apply to it, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIOPS.StorageTypes.html#USER_PIOPS.Autoscaling\&quot;&gt; Managing capacity automatically with Amazon RDS storage autoscaling&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **certificateRotationRestart** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether the DB instance is restarted when you rotate your SSL/TLS certificate.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;By default, the DB instance is restarted when you rotate your SSL/TLS certificate. The certificate is not updated until the DB instance is restarted.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;important&gt; &lt;p&gt;Set this parameter only if you are &lt;i&gt;not&lt;/i&gt; using SSL/TLS to connect to the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/important&gt; &lt;p&gt;If you are using SSL/TLS to connect to the DB instance, follow the appropriate instructions for your DB engine to rotate your SSL/TLS certificate:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information about rotating your SSL/TLS certificate for RDS DB engines, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/UsingWithRDS.SSL-certificate-rotation.html\&quot;&gt; Rotating Your SSL/TLS Certificate.&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information about rotating your SSL/TLS certificate for Aurora DB engines, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/UsingWithRDS.SSL-certificate-rotation.html\&quot;&gt; Rotating Your SSL/TLS Certificate&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **replicaMode** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;A value that sets the open mode of a replica database to either mounted or read-only.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;Currently, this parameter is only supported for Oracle DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/note&gt; &lt;p&gt;Mounted DB replicas are included in Oracle Enterprise Edition. The main use case for mounted replicas is cross-Region disaster recovery. The primary database doesn&#39;t use Active Data Guard to transmit information to the mounted replica. Because it doesn&#39;t accept user connections, a mounted replica can&#39;t serve a read-only workload. For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/oracle-read-replicas.html\&quot;&gt;Working with Oracle Read Replicas for Amazon RDS&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] [enum: open-read-only, mounted] |
| **enableCustomerOwnedIp** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to enable a customer-owned IP address (CoIP) for an RDS on Outposts DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;A &lt;i&gt;CoIP&lt;/i&gt; provides local or external connectivity to resources in your Outpost subnets through your on-premises network. For some use cases, a CoIP can provide lower latency for connections to the DB instance from outside of its virtual private cloud (VPC) on your local network.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information about RDS on Outposts, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-on-outposts.html\&quot;&gt;Working with Amazon RDS on Amazon Web Services Outposts&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information about CoIPs, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/outposts/latest/userguide/routing.html#ip-addressing\&quot;&gt;Customer-owned IP addresses&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Web Services Outposts User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **awsBackupRecoveryPointArn** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the recovery point in Amazon Web Services Backup.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **automationMode** | **String**| The automation mode of the RDS Custom DB instance. If &lt;code&gt;full&lt;/code&gt;, the DB instance automates monitoring and instance recovery. If &lt;code&gt;all paused&lt;/code&gt;, the instance pauses automation for the duration set by &lt;code&gt;ResumeFullAutomationModeMinutes&lt;/code&gt;. | [optional] [enum: full, all-paused] |
| **resumeFullAutomationModeMinutes** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The number of minutes to pause the automation. When the time period ends, RDS Custom resumes full automation.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;60&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be at least 60.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be no more than 1,440.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **networkType** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The network type of the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The network type is determined by the &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroup&lt;/code&gt; specified for the DB instance. A &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroup&lt;/code&gt; can support only the IPv4 protocol or the IPv4 and the IPv6 protocols (&lt;code&gt;DUAL&lt;/code&gt;).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_VPC.WorkingWithRDSInstanceinaVPC.html\&quot;&gt; Working with a DB instance in a VPC&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid Values: &lt;code&gt;IPV4 | DUAL&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **storageThroughput** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The storage throughput value for the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting applies only to the &lt;code&gt;gp3&lt;/code&gt; storage type.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting doesn&#39;t apply to Amazon Aurora or RDS Custom DB instances.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **manageMasterUserPassword** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to manage the master user password with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the DB instance doesn&#39;t manage the master user password with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager, you can turn on this management. In this case, you can&#39;t specify &lt;code&gt;MasterUserPassword&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the DB instance already manages the master user password with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager, and you specify that the master user password is not managed with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager, then you must specify &lt;code&gt;MasterUserPassword&lt;/code&gt;. In this case, Amazon RDS deletes the secret and uses the new password for the master user specified by &lt;code&gt;MasterUserPassword&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html\&quot;&gt;Password management with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can&#39;t manage the master user password with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager if &lt;code&gt;MasterUserPassword&lt;/code&gt; is specified.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |
| **rotateMasterUserPassword** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies whether to rotate the secret managed by Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager for the master user password.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This setting is valid only if the master user password is managed by RDS in Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager for the DB cluster. The secret value contains the updated password.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html\&quot;&gt;Password management with Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;You must apply the change immediately when rotating the master user password.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; | [optional] |

<a id="gETModifyDBSnapshotAttribute"></a>
# **gETModifyDBSnapshotAttribute**
> ModifyDBSnapshotAttributeResult gETModifyDBSnapshotAttribute(dbSnapshotIdentifier, attributeName, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, valuesToAdd, valuesToRemove)



&lt;p&gt;Adds an attribute and values to, or removes an attribute and values from, a manual DB snapshot.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;To share a manual DB snapshot with other Amazon Web Services accounts, specify &lt;code&gt;restore&lt;/code&gt; as the &lt;code&gt;AttributeName&lt;/code&gt; and use the &lt;code&gt;ValuesToAdd&lt;/code&gt; parameter to add a list of IDs of the Amazon Web Services accounts that are authorized to restore the manual DB snapshot. Uses the value &lt;code&gt;all&lt;/code&gt; to make the manual DB snapshot public, which means it can be copied or restored by all Amazon Web Services accounts.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;Don&#39;t add the &lt;code&gt;all&lt;/code&gt; value for any manual DB snapshots that contain private information that you don&#39;t want available to all Amazon Web Services accounts.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/note&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the manual DB snapshot is encrypted, it can be shared, but only by specifying a list of authorized Amazon Web Services account IDs for the &lt;code&gt;ValuesToAdd&lt;/code&gt; parameter. You can&#39;t use &lt;code&gt;all&lt;/code&gt; as a value for that parameter in this case.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;To view which Amazon Web Services accounts have access to copy or restore a manual DB snapshot, or whether a manual DB snapshot public or private, use the &lt;a&gt;DescribeDBSnapshotAttributes&lt;/a&gt; API operation. The accounts are returned as values for the &lt;code&gt;restore&lt;/code&gt; attribute.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Promotes a read replica DB instance to a standalone DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Backup duration is a function of the amount of changes to the database since the previous backup. If you plan to promote a read replica to a standalone instance, we recommend that you enable backups and complete at least one backup prior to promotion. In addition, a read replica cannot be promoted to a standalone instance when it is in the &lt;code&gt;backing-up&lt;/code&gt; status. If you have enabled backups on your read replica, configure the automated backup window so that daily backups do not interfere with read replica promotion.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;This command doesn&#39;t apply to Aurora MySQL, Aurora PostgreSQL, or RDS Custom.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;/note&gt;

<a id="gETResetDBParameterGroup"></a>
# **gETResetDBParameterGroup**
> DBParameterGroupNameMessage gETResetDBParameterGroup(dbParameterGroupName, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, resetAllParameters, parameters)



Modifies the parameters of a DB parameter group to the engine/system default value. To reset specific parameters, provide a list of the following: &lt;code&gt;ParameterName&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;ApplyMethod&lt;/code&gt;. To reset the entire DB parameter group, specify the &lt;code&gt;DBParameterGroup&lt;/code&gt; name and &lt;code&gt;ResetAllParameters&lt;/code&gt; parameters. # **gETRestoreDBClusterFromS3**
> RestoreDBClusterFromS3Result gETRestoreDBClusterFromS3(dbClusterIdentifier, engine, masterUsername, sourceEngine, sourceEngineVersion, s3BucketName, s3IngestionRoleArn, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, availabilityZones, backupRetentionPeriod, characterSetName, databaseName, dbClusterParameterGroupName, vpcSecurityGroupIds, dbSubnetGroupName, engineVersion, port, masterUserPassword, optionGroupName, preferredBackupWindow, preferredMaintenanceWindow, tags, storageEncrypted, kmsKeyId, enableIAMDatabaseAuthentication, s3Prefix, backtrackWindow, enableCloudwatchLogsExports, deletionProtection, copyTagsToSnapshot, domain, domainIAMRoleName, serverlessV2ScalingConfiguration, networkType, manageMasterUserPassword, masterUserSecretKmsKeyId, storageType)



&lt;p&gt;Creates an Amazon Aurora DB cluster from MySQL data stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. Amazon RDS must be authorized to access the Amazon S3 bucket and the data must be created using the Percona XtraBackup utility as described in &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraMySQL.Migrating.ExtMySQL.html#AuroraMySQL.Migrating.ExtMySQL.S3\&quot;&gt; Migrating Data from MySQL by Using an Amazon S3 Bucket&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;This action only restores the DB cluster, not the DB instances for that DB cluster. You must invoke the &lt;code&gt;CreateDBInstance&lt;/code&gt; action to create DB instances for the restored DB cluster, specifying the identifier of the restored DB cluster in &lt;code&gt;DBClusterIdentifier&lt;/code&gt;. You can create DB instances only after the &lt;code&gt;RestoreDBClusterFromS3&lt;/code&gt; action has completed and the DB cluster is available.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/note&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on Amazon Aurora, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html\&quot;&gt; What is Amazon Aurora?&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;This action only applies to Aurora DB clusters. The source DB engine must be MySQL.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/note&gt;

# **gETRestoreDBClusterFromSnapshot**
> RestoreDBClusterFromSnapshotResult gETRestoreDBClusterFromSnapshot(dbClusterIdentifier, snapshotIdentifier, engine, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, availabilityZones, engineVersion, port, dbSubnetGroupName, databaseName, optionGroupName, vpcSecurityGroupIds, tags, kmsKeyId, enableIAMDatabaseAuthentication, backtrackWindow, enableCloudwatchLogsExports, engineMode, scalingConfiguration, dbClusterParameterGroupName, deletionProtection, copyTagsToSnapshot, domain, domainIAMRoleName, dbClusterInstanceClass, storageType, iops, publiclyAccessible, serverlessV2ScalingConfiguration, networkType)



&lt;p&gt;Creates a new DB cluster from a DB snapshot or DB cluster snapshot.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The target DB cluster is created from the source snapshot with a default configuration. If you don&#39;t specify a security group, the new DB cluster is associated with the default security group.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;This action only restores the DB cluster, not the DB instances for that DB cluster. You must invoke the &lt;code&gt;CreateDBInstance&lt;/code&gt; action to create DB instances for the restored DB cluster, specifying the identifier of the restored DB cluster in &lt;code&gt;DBClusterIdentifier&lt;/code&gt;. You can create DB instances only after the &lt;code&gt;RestoreDBClusterFromSnapshot&lt;/code&gt; action has completed and the DB cluster is available.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/note&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on Amazon Aurora DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html\&quot;&gt; What is Amazon Aurora?&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on Multi-AZ DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/multi-az-db-clusters-concepts.html\&quot;&gt; Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt;

in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;MySQL&lt;/b&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;See &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_MySQL.html#MySQL.Concepts.VersionMgmt\&quot;&gt;Amazon RDS for MySQL&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;PostgreSQL&lt;/b&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;See &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_PostgreSQL.html#PostgreSQL.Concepts\&quot;&gt;Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL versions and extensions&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **port** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The port number on which the new DB cluster accepts connections.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints: This value must be &lt;code&gt;1150-65535&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: The same port as the original DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **dbSubnetGroupName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The name of the DB subnet group to use for the new DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints: If supplied, must match the name of an existing DB subnet group.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Example: &lt;code&gt;mydbsubnetgroup&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **databaseName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The database name for the restored DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **optionGroupName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The name of the option group to use for the restored DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;DB clusters are associated with a default option group that can&#39;t be modified.&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **vpcSecurityGroupIds** | [**List&lt;String&gt;**](String.md)| &lt;p&gt;A list of VPC security groups that the new DB cluster will belong to.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **tags** | [**List&lt;Tag&gt;**](Tag.md)| &lt;p&gt;The tags to be assigned to the restored DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **kmsKeyId** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier to use when restoring an encrypted DB cluster from a DB snapshot or DB cluster snapshot.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier is the key ARN, key ID, alias ARN, or alias name for the KMS key. To use a KMS key in a different Amazon Web Services account, specify the key ARN or alias ARN.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When you don&#39;t specify a value for the &lt;code&gt;KmsKeyId&lt;/code&gt; parameter, then the following occurs:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the DB snapshot or DB cluster snapshot in &lt;code&gt;SnapshotIdentifier&lt;/code&gt; is encrypted, then the restored DB cluster is encrypted using the KMS key that was used to encrypt the DB snapshot or DB cluster snapshot.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the DB snapshot or DB cluster snapshot in &lt;code&gt;SnapshotIdentifier&lt;/code&gt; isn&#39;t encrypted, then the restored DB cluster isn&#39;t encrypted.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **enableIAMDatabaseAuthentication** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;A value that indicates whether to enable mapping of Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management (IAM) accounts to database accounts. By default, mapping isn&#39;t enabled.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/UsingWithRDS.IAMDBAuth.html\&quot;&gt; IAM Database Authentication&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **backtrackWindow** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The target backtrack window, in seconds. To disable backtracking, set this value to 0.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;Currently, Backtrack is only supported for Aurora MySQL DB clusters.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/note&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: 0&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If specified, this value must be set to a number from 0 to 259,200 (72 hours).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **enableCloudwatchLogsExports** | [**List&lt;String&gt;**](String.md)| &lt;p&gt;The list of logs that the restored DB cluster is to export to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The values in the list depend on the DB engine being used.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;RDS for MySQL&lt;/b&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Possible values are &lt;code&gt;error&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;general&lt;/code&gt;, and &lt;code&gt;slowquery&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;RDS for PostgreSQL&lt;/b&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Possible values are &lt;code&gt;postgresql&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;upgrade&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;Aurora MySQL&lt;/b&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Possible values are &lt;code&gt;audit&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;error&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;general&lt;/code&gt;, and &lt;code&gt;slowquery&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;Aurora PostgreSQL&lt;/b&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Possible value is &lt;code&gt;postgresql&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information about exporting CloudWatch Logs for Amazon RDS, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_LogAccess.html#USER_LogAccess.Procedural.UploadtoCloudWatch\&quot;&gt;Publishing Database Logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information about exporting CloudWatch Logs for Amazon Aurora, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/USER_LogAccess.html#USER_LogAccess.Procedural.UploadtoCloudWatch\&quot;&gt;Publishing Database Logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **engineMode** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The DB engine mode of the DB cluster, either &lt;code&gt;provisioned&lt;/code&gt; or &lt;code&gt;serverless&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/APIReference/API_CreateDBCluster.html\&quot;&gt; CreateDBCluster&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **scalingConfiguration** | [**GETCreateDBClusterScalingConfigurationParameter**](.md)| &lt;p&gt;For DB clusters in &lt;code&gt;serverless&lt;/code&gt; DB engine mode, the scaling properties of the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **dbClusterParameterGroupName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The name of the DB cluster parameter group to associate with this DB cluster. If this argument is omitted, the default DB cluster parameter group for the specified engine is used.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If supplied, must match the name of an existing default DB cluster parameter group.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Must be 1 to 255 letters, numbers, or hyphens.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;First character must be a letter.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;Can&#39;t end with a hyphen or contain two consecutive hyphens.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **deletionProtection** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;A value that indicates whether the DB cluster has deletion protection enabled. The database can&#39;t be deleted when deletion protection is enabled. By default, deletion protection isn&#39;t enabled.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **copyTagsToSnapshot** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;A value that indicates whether to copy all tags from the restored DB cluster to snapshots of the restored DB cluster. The default is not to copy them.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **domain** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;Specify the Active Directory directory ID to restore the DB cluster in. The domain must be created prior to this operation. Currently, only MySQL, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle, and PostgreSQL DB instances can be created in an Active Directory Domain.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/kerberos-authentication.html\&quot;&gt; Kerberos Authentication&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **domainIAMRoleName** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;Specify the name of the IAM role to be used when making API calls to the Directory Service.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **dbClusterInstanceClass** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The compute and memory capacity of the each DB instance in the Multi-AZ DB cluster, for example db.m6gd.xlarge. Not all DB instance classes are available in all Amazon Web Services Regions, or for all database engines.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For the full list of DB instance classes, and availability for your engine, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.DBInstanceClass.html\&quot;&gt;DB Instance Class&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **storageType** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies the storage type to be associated with the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When specified for a Multi-AZ DB cluster, a value for the &lt;code&gt;Iops&lt;/code&gt; parameter is required.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid values: &lt;code&gt;aurora&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;aurora-iopt1&lt;/code&gt; (Aurora DB clusters); &lt;code&gt;io1&lt;/code&gt; (Multi-AZ DB clusters)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;aurora&lt;/code&gt; (Aurora DB clusters); &lt;code&gt;io1&lt;/code&gt; (Multi-AZ DB clusters)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **iops** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The amount of Provisioned IOPS (input/output operations per second) to be initially allocated for each DB instance in the Multi-AZ DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For information about valid IOPS values, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_Storage.html#USER_PIOPS\&quot;&gt;Amazon RDS Provisioned IOPS storage&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints: Must be a multiple between .5 and 50 of the storage amount for the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **publiclyAccessible** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;A value that indicates whether the DB cluster is publicly accessible.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When the DB cluster is publicly accessible, its Domain Name System (DNS) endpoint resolves to the private IP address from within the DB cluster&#39;s virtual private cloud (VPC). It resolves to the public IP address from outside of the DB cluster&#39;s VPC. Access to the DB cluster is ultimately controlled by the security group it uses. That public access is not permitted if the security group assigned to the DB cluster doesn&#39;t permit it.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When the DB cluster isn&#39;t publicly accessible, it is an internal DB cluster with a DNS name that resolves to a private IP address.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: The default behavior varies depending on whether &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroupName&lt;/code&gt; is specified.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroupName&lt;/code&gt; isn&#39;t specified, and &lt;code&gt;PubliclyAccessible&lt;/code&gt; isn&#39;t specified, the following applies:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the default VPC in the target Region doesn’t have an internet gateway attached to it, the DB cluster is private.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the default VPC in the target Region has an internet gateway attached to it, the DB cluster is public.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroupName&lt;/code&gt; is specified, and &lt;code&gt;PubliclyAccessible&lt;/code&gt; isn&#39;t specified, the following applies:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the subnets are part of a VPC that doesn’t have an internet gateway attached to it, the DB cluster is private.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the subnets are part of a VPC that has an internet gateway attached to it, the DB cluster is public.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **serverlessV2ScalingConfiguration** | [**GETCreateDBClusterServerlessV2ScalingConfigurationParameter**](.md)|  | [optional] |
| **networkType** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The network type of the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid values:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;IPV4&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;DUAL&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;The network type is determined by the &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroup&lt;/code&gt; specified for the DB cluster. A &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroup&lt;/code&gt; can support only the IPv4 protocol or the IPv4 and the IPv6 protocols (&lt;code&gt;DUAL&lt;/code&gt;).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/USER_VPC.WorkingWithRDSInstanceinaVPC.html\&quot;&gt; Working with a DB instance in a VPC&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |

<a id="gETRestoreDBClusterToPointInTime"></a>
# **gETRestoreDBClusterToPointInTime**
> RestoreDBClusterToPointInTimeResult gETRestoreDBClusterToPointInTime(dbClusterIdentifier, action, version, xAmzContentSha256, xAmzDate, xAmzAlgorithm, xAmzCredential, xAmzSecurityToken, xAmzSignature, xAmzSignedHeaders, restoreType, sourceDBClusterIdentifier, restoreToTime, useLatestRestorableTime, port, dbSubnetGroupName, optionGroupName, vpcSecurityGroupIds, tags, kmsKeyId, enableIAMDatabaseAuthentication, backtrackWindow, enableCloudwatchLogsExports, dbClusterParameterGroupName, deletionProtection, copyTagsToSnapshot, domain, domainIAMRoleName, scalingConfiguration, engineMode, dbClusterInstanceClass, storageType, publiclyAccessible, iops, serverlessV2ScalingConfiguration, networkType, sourceDbClusterResourceId)



&lt;p&gt;Restores a DB cluster to an arbitrary point in time. Users can restore to any point in time before &lt;code&gt;LatestRestorableTime&lt;/code&gt; for up to &lt;code&gt;BackupRetentionPeriod&lt;/code&gt; days. The target DB cluster is created from the source DB cluster with the same configuration as the original DB cluster, except that the new DB cluster is created with the default DB security group.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;note&gt; &lt;p&gt;For Aurora, this action only restores the DB cluster, not the DB instances for that DB cluster. You must invoke the &lt;code&gt;CreateDBInstance&lt;/code&gt; action to create DB instances for the restored DB cluster, specifying the identifier of the restored DB cluster in &lt;code&gt;DBClusterIdentifier&lt;/code&gt;. You can create DB instances only after the &lt;code&gt;RestoreDBClusterToPointInTime&lt;/code&gt; action has completed and the DB cluster is available.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/note&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on Amazon Aurora DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html\&quot;&gt; What is Amazon Aurora?&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information on Multi-AZ DB clusters, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/multi-az-db-clusters-concepts.html\&quot;&gt; Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt;

```java

import org.openapitools.client.models.*;
import org.openapitools.client.api.DefaultApi;

public class Example {
  public static void main(String[] args) {
    ApiClient defaultClient = Configuration.getDefaultApiClient();
    defaultClient.setBasePath("http://rds.us-east-1.amazonaws.com");
    
    // Configure API key authorization: hmac
    ApiKeyAuth hmac = (ApiKeyAuth) defaultClient.getAuthentication("hmac");
    hmac.setApiKey("YOUR API KEY");
    // Uncomment the following line to set a prefix for the API key, e.g. "Token" (defaults to null)
    //hmac.setApiKeyPrefix("Token");

    DefaultApi apiInstance = new DefaultApi(defaultClient);
    String dbClusterIdentifier = "dbClusterIdentifier_example"; // String | <p>The name of the new DB cluster to be created.</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Must contain from 1 to 63 letters, numbers, or hyphens</p> </li> <li> <p>First character must be a letter</p> </li> <li> <p>Can't end with a hyphen or contain two consecutive hyphens</p> </li> </ul> <p>Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters</p>
    String action = "RestoreDBClusterToPointInTime"; // String | 
    String version = "2014-10-31"; // String | 
    String xAmzContentSha256 = "xAmzContentSha256_example"; // String | 
    String xAmzDate = "xAmzDate_example"; // String | 
    String xAmzAlgorithm = "xAmzAlgorithm_example"; // String | 
    String xAmzCredential = "xAmzCredential_example"; // String | 
    String xAmzSecurityToken = "xAmzSecurityToken_example"; // String | 
    String xAmzSignature = "xAmzSignature_example"; // String | 
    String xAmzSignedHeaders = "xAmzSignedHeaders_example"; // String | 
    String restoreType = "restoreType_example"; // String | <p>The type of restore to be performed. You can specify one of the following values:</p> <ul> <li> <p> <code>full-copy</code> - The new DB cluster is restored as a full copy of the source DB cluster.</p> </li> <li> <p> <code>copy-on-write</code> - The new DB cluster is restored as a clone of the source DB cluster.</p> </li> </ul> <p>If you don't specify a <code>RestoreType</code> value, then the new DB cluster is restored as a full copy of the source DB cluster.</p> <p>Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters</p>
    String sourceDBClusterIdentifier = "sourceDBClusterIdentifier_example"; // String | <p>The identifier of the source DB cluster from which to restore.</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Must match the identifier of an existing DBCluster.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters</p>
    OffsetDateTime restoreToTime = OffsetDateTime.now(); // OffsetDateTime | <p>The date and time to restore the DB cluster to.</p> <p>Valid Values: Value must be a time in Universal Coordinated Time (UTC) format</p> <p>Constraints:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Must be before the latest restorable time for the DB instance</p> </li> <li> <p>Must be specified if <code>UseLatestRestorableTime</code> parameter isn't provided</p> </li> <li> <p>Can't be specified if the <code>UseLatestRestorableTime</code> parameter is enabled</p> </li> <li> <p>Can't be specified if the <code>RestoreType</code> parameter is <code>copy-on-write</code> </p> </li> </ul> <p>Example: <code>2015-03-07T23:45:00Z</code> </p> <p>Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters</p>
    Boolean useLatestRestorableTime = true; // Boolean | <p>A value that indicates whether to restore the DB cluster to the latest restorable backup time. By default, the DB cluster isn't restored to the latest restorable backup time.</p> <p>Constraints: Can't be specified if <code>RestoreToTime</code> parameter is provided.</p> <p>Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters</p>
    Integer port = 56; // Integer | <p>The port number on which the new DB cluster accepts connections.</p> <p>Constraints: A value from <code>1150-65535</code>.</p> <p>Default: The default port for the engine.</p> <p>Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters</p>
    String dbSubnetGroupName = "dbSubnetGroupName_example"; // String | <p>The DB subnet group name to use for the new DB cluster.</p> <p>Constraints: If supplied, must match the name of an existing DBSubnetGroup.</p> <p>Example: <code>mydbsubnetgroup</code> </p> <p>Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters</p>
    String optionGroupName = "optionGroupName_example"; // String | <p>The name of the option group for the new DB cluster.</p> <p>DB clusters are associated with a default option group that can't be modified.</p>
```

| **storageType** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;Specifies the storage type to be associated with the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When specified for a Multi-AZ DB cluster, a value for the &lt;code&gt;Iops&lt;/code&gt; parameter is required.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid values: &lt;code&gt;aurora&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;aurora-iopt1&lt;/code&gt; (Aurora DB clusters); &lt;code&gt;io1&lt;/code&gt; (Multi-AZ DB clusters)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: &lt;code&gt;aurora&lt;/code&gt; (Aurora DB clusters); &lt;code&gt;io1&lt;/code&gt; (Multi-AZ DB clusters)&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters and Multi-AZ DB clusters&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **publiclyAccessible** | **Boolean**| &lt;p&gt;A value that indicates whether the DB cluster is publicly accessible.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When the DB cluster is publicly accessible, its Domain Name System (DNS) endpoint resolves to the private IP address from within the DB cluster&#39;s virtual private cloud (VPC). It resolves to the public IP address from outside of the DB cluster&#39;s VPC. Access to the DB cluster is ultimately controlled by the security group it uses. That public access is not permitted if the security group assigned to the DB cluster doesn&#39;t permit it.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When the DB cluster isn&#39;t publicly accessible, it is an internal DB cluster with a DNS name that resolves to a private IP address.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Default: The default behavior varies depending on whether &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroupName&lt;/code&gt; is specified.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroupName&lt;/code&gt; isn&#39;t specified, and &lt;code&gt;PubliclyAccessible&lt;/code&gt; isn&#39;t specified, the following applies:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the default VPC in the target Region doesn’t have an internet gateway attached to it, the DB cluster is private.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the default VPC in the target Region has an internet gateway attached to it, the DB cluster is public.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;If &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroupName&lt;/code&gt; is specified, and &lt;code&gt;PubliclyAccessible&lt;/code&gt; isn&#39;t specified, the following applies:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the subnets are part of a VPC that doesn’t have an internet gateway attached to it, the DB cluster is private.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt;If the subnets are part of a VPC that has an internet gateway attached to it, the DB cluster is public.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **iops** | **Integer**| &lt;p&gt;The amount of Provisioned IOPS (input/output operations per second) to be initially allocated for each DB instance in the Multi-AZ DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For information about valid IOPS values, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_Storage.html#USER_PIOPS\&quot;&gt;Amazon RDS Provisioned IOPS storage&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon RDS User Guide&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Constraints: Must be a multiple between .5 and 50 of the storage amount for the DB instance.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Multi-AZ DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **serverlessV2ScalingConfiguration** | [**GETCreateDBClusterServerlessV2ScalingConfigurationParameter**](.md)|  | [optional] |
| **networkType** | **String**| &lt;p&gt;The network type of the DB cluster.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid values:&lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;IPV4&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;code&gt;DUAL&lt;/code&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt;The network type is determined by the &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroup&lt;/code&gt; specified for the DB cluster. A &lt;code&gt;DBSubnetGroup&lt;/code&gt; can support only the IPv4 protocol or the IPv4 and the IPv6 protocols (&lt;code&gt;DUAL&lt;/code&gt;).&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For more information, see &lt;a href&#x3D;\&quot;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/USER_VPC.WorkingWithRDSInstanceinaVPC.html\&quot;&gt; Working with a DB instance in a VPC&lt;/a&gt; in the &lt;i&gt;Amazon Aurora User Guide.&lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Valid for: Aurora DB clusters only&lt;/p&gt; | [optional] |
| **sourceDbClusterResourceId** | **String**| The resource ID of the source DB cluster from which to restore. | [optional] |
